ledger.clause:
8.3 Properties listed for sale (§11.5)
STD-8.8 A property is considered listed for sale under §11.5 if it has been listed for sale in the last six months, measured from (a) the last date of being listed to (b) the Application Date. \[G §11.5, p. 12\]

STD-8.9 Loans on such properties will be considered under the following characteristics: the property is not in default or otherwise delinquent on lien(s); for investment properties, the subject must be occupied by a tenant and may not be vacant; the loan must qualify as either (a) ≥ 1.0 DSCR or (b) 43% maximum DTI (Q-14); a prepayment penalty of at least three (3) years is required unless the property is in a state that does not allow prepayment penalties; twenty-four (24) months of reserves are required, and cash-in-hand may be considered if otherwise consistent with the Guide; the loan must have a fully amortizing term, interest only is not available; the maximum LTV / CLTV is 65% based on the lesser of (a) appraised value or (b) lowest recent listing price; no subordinate financing is allowed; impounds are required. \[G §11.5, pp. 11–12\]

condition.purpose: Determine whether a loan on a property listed for sale in the last six months meets the stated loan characteristics.
steps: Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Review the loan application, appraisal report, listing history, rent documentation, and reserve documentation.
Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: Establish that the property was listed for sale in the last six months under §11.5.

Step 3 - Validation and Verification: Verify each applicable listed-property characteristic: not in default or otherwise delinquent on lien(s); investment property occupied by a tenant and not vacant; qualifies as either ≥ 1.0 DSCR or 43% maximum DTI (Q-14); prepayment penalty of at least three (3) years unless the property is in a state that does not allow prepayment penalties; twenty-four (24) months of reserves, with cash-in-hand considered if otherwise consistent with the Guide; fully amortizing term and no interest only; maximum LTV / CLTV 65% based on the lesser of appraised value or lowest recent listing price; no subordinate financing; impounds required.
Step 4 - Final Determination: Determine whether each applicable listed-property characteristic is met.
checks: The property is not in default or otherwise delinquent on lien(s).
For an investment property, the subject is occupied by a tenant and is not vacant.
The loan qualifies as either ≥ 1.0 DSCR or 43% maximum DTI (Q-14).
A prepayment penalty of at least three (3) years applies unless the property is in a state that does not allow prepayment penalties.
Twenty-four (24) months of reserves are held; cash-in-hand may be considered if otherwise consistent with the Guide.
The loan has a fully amortizing term and is not interest only.
Maximum LTV / CLTV is 65% based on the lesser of appraised value or lowest recent listing price.
No subordinate financing is allowed.
Impounds are in place.

outcomes.criterion: Every applicable listed-property characteristic is met.
A required condition remains to be cleared.
A listed-property characteristic is not met.
The property was not listed for sale in the last six months.

STD-8.8 A property is considered listed for sale under §11.5 if it has been listed for sale in the last six months, measured from (a) the last date of being listed to (b) the Application Date. \[G §11.5, p. 12\]

STD-8.9 Loans on such properties will be considered under the following characteristics: the property is not in default or otherwise delinquent on lien(s); for investment properties, the subject must be occupied by a tenant and may not be vacant; the loan must qualify as either (a) ≥ 1.0 DSCR or (b) 43% maximum DTI (Q-14); a prepayment penalty of at least three (3) years is required unless the property is in a state that does not allow prepayment penalties; twenty-four (24) months of reserves are required, and cash-in-hand may be considered if otherwise consistent with the Guide; the loan must have a fully amortizing term, interest only is not available; the maximum LTV / CLTV is 65% based on the lesser of (a) appraised value or (b) lowest recent listing price; no subordinate financing is allowed; impounds are required. \[G §11.5, pp. 11–12\]

condition.purpose: Determine whether the stated vacant-property cash-out refinance conditions are met, including the stated amount and ownership limits.
steps: Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Review the loan application, appraisal report, and reserve documentation.
Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: Establish that the property is vacant and the transaction is cash-out refinance.

Loans of $1,500,000 or more, and how the 15 months are measured, require Acra confirmation (Q-10).
Step 4 - Final Determination: Determine whether the stated conditions are met and refer the specified unresolved terms for confirmation.
checks: FICO is at least 700.
DSCR is ≥ 1.15.
A ≥ 3-year PPP applies where allowable.
The loan is not interest-only.
Impounds are in place.
Reserves are at least 6 months.
For loan amounts under $1,500,000, CLTV does not exceed 60%.
Ownership is at least 15 months.
Loans of $1,500,000 or more, and how the 15 months are measured, are referred for Acra confirmation (Q-10).

condition.purpose: Determine whether the applicant contributes the required minimum of own funds when gifting is allowed and used.
steps: Initial Document Review: Review available documentation of the applicant's transaction contribution and the source and seasoning of funds.
Eligibility Verification: Determine whether gift funds are being used for the transaction.

Validation and Verification: If gifting is used, verify that the applicant contributes a minimum of 10% of the purchase price from the applicant's own sourced and seasoned funds. Gift documentation requirements are in the Seller's Guide gift-fund section (Appendix B), which is not reproduced here.
Final Determination: Determine whether the required own-funds contribution is documented, or whether the gifting condition does not apply.
checks: If gifting is used, the applicant contributes a minimum of 10% of the purchase price from the applicant's own sourced and seasoned funds.

outcomes.criterion: Every applicable step is met and the own-funds contribution check holds.
Gift funds are used and the required gift-fund documentation requirements from Appendix B remain to be cleared.
A step is not met or the own-funds contribution check does not hold.
Gifting is not used for the transaction.

ledger.clause:
1.2 Loan amount, contributions and gifts
STD-1.10 Minimum loan amount \$100,000; maximum loan amount \$3,000,000; loan amount to be in \$50 increments. \[S: Loan Amount\]

STD-1.11 Seller concession / other contributions: limited to 3% of the sale price. \[S: Loan Amount\]

STD-1.12 Gifting is allowed and “requires borrower to contribute a minimum of 10% of the purchase price consisting of their own funds”; §8.7 states the contribution as the applicant's “own sourced and seasoned funds”. Gift documentation requirements are in the Seller's Guide gift-fund section, not reproduced (Appendix B). \[S: Loan Amount; G §8.7, p. 12\]

9.1 Gift funds, funds to close and seasoning
STD-9.1 Gift funds, investment property or second homes: applicant(s) are required to contribute a portion of their own sourced and seasoned funds to the transaction at a minimum of 10% of the purchase price. Gift documentation requirements are in the Seller's Guide gift-fund section (Appendix B). \[G §8.7, p. 12; S: Loan Amount\]

STD-9.2 Verification of the seasoning of funds to close is required on loans over 70% CLTV for consumer transactions, or business purpose loans where funds to close are over \$50,000 and over 70% CLTV. Whether any loan on this program is a consumer transaction: Acra confirmation requested → Q-27. \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

STD-9.3 Where the account(s) serving as the source of funds must be verified, verification may include a copy of the borrower's bank statement(s) for the most recent month(s), or a VOD reflecting a current and average balance for the most recent month(s). \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

STD-9.4 “All transactions require a minimum of 30-days documentation.” Whether any seasoning period applies to domestic funds beyond this documentation minimum: Acra confirmation requested → Q-12. \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

STD-9.5 “In contrast to the above, but consistent with §3.10.1 of this Guide, funds held in a foreign bank / currency will need to be repatriated at minimum three (3) business days prior to Closing and Foreign Nationals, regardless of LTV / CLTV, need to document a minimum of 60 days seasoning.” Whether the repatriation requirement applies to any borrower holding funds abroad or only to foreign nationals, and what evidence applies: Acra confirmation requested → Q-12. \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

9. Assets, funds to close and reserves
Gift funds, seasoning and verification of funds come from §8.7 and §8.4 of the excerpt. Reserve requirements are stated by trigger in both sources and are collected in one table without addition.

9.2 Reserves by trigger, as stated
STD-9.6 The sources state reserves only for the situations below, and state the payment basis only where shown. The base requirement where no trigger applies, the payment basis where only “months” is stated, permitted sources, whether overlapping triggers are cumulative, and whether reserves substituted for rent loss insurance are additional: Acra confirmation requested → Q-07. \[S; G\]

| **Trigger** | **Reserves as printed** | **Source** |
|----|----|----|

9.1 Gift funds, funds to close and seasoning
STD-9.1 Gift funds, investment property or second homes: applicant(s) are required to contribute a portion of their own sourced and seasoned funds to the transaction at a minimum of 10% of the purchase price. Gift documentation requirements are in the Seller's Guide gift-fund section (Appendix B). \[G §8.7, p. 12; S: Loan Amount\]

STD-9.2 Verification of the seasoning of funds to close is required on loans over 70% CLTV for consumer transactions, or business purpose loans where funds to close are over \$50,000 and over 70% CLTV. Whether any loan on this program is a consumer transaction: Acra confirmation requested → Q-27. \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

STD-9.3 Where the account(s) serving as the source of funds must be verified, verification may include a copy of the borrower's bank statement(s) for the most recent month(s), or a VOD reflecting a current and average balance for the most recent month(s). \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

STD-9.4 “All transactions require a minimum of 30-days documentation.” Whether any seasoning period applies to domestic funds beyond this documentation minimum: Acra confirmation requested → Q-12. \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

STD-9.5 “In contrast to the above, but consistent with §3.10.1 of this Guide, funds held in a foreign bank / currency will need to be repatriated at minimum three (3) business days prior to Closing and Foreign Nationals, regardless of LTV / CLTV, need to document a minimum of 60 days seasoning.” Whether the repatriation requirement applies to any borrower holding funds abroad or only to foreign nationals, and what evidence applies: Acra confirmation requested → Q-12. \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

9. Assets, funds to close and reserves
Gift funds, seasoning and verification of funds come from §8.7 and §8.4 of the excerpt. Reserve requirements are stated by trigger in both sources and are collected in one table without addition.

5.2 Assets held in foreign accounts
STD-5.6 Assets held / foreign accounts must be verified in U.S. Dollar equivalency at the current exchange rate via www.xe.com or the Wall Street Journal conversion table. \[G §3.10, p. 6\]

STD-5.7 Sufficient funds to close must be on deposit with the Escrow / Closing Agent at least three (3) business days (including Saturdays for this calculation) prior to any closing date. \[G §3.10, p. 6\]

STD-5.8 A copy of the two (2) most recent statements of that account is required. If the funds are not seasoned a minimum of sixty (60) days, a letter of explanation is required along with the information to comprise a sixty (60) day chain of funds. Bank statements in any language other than English must be translated into English. \[G §3.10, p. 6\]

STD-5.9 Per §8.4, Foreign Nationals, regardless of LTV / CLTV, need to document a minimum of 60 days seasoning, and funds held in a foreign bank / currency must be repatriated at minimum three (3) business days prior to Closing (STD-9.5). \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

Gift documentation requirements are in the Seller's Guide gift-fund section (Appendix B). \[G §8.7, p. 12; S: Loan Amount\]

STD-9.2 Verification of the seasoning of funds to close is required on loans over 70% CLTV for consumer transactions, or business purpose loans where funds to close are over \$50,000 and over 70% CLTV. Whether any loan on this program is a consumer transaction: Acra confirmation requested → Q-27. \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

6.1 Entity eligibility and guarantees
STD-6.1 Business Entities are eligible for financing on business purpose transactions (investment properties exclusively). \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.2 Acra will lend to, and require that title to the collateral be held, either (i) directly by an individual person(s) or (ii) by an entity acceptable to Acra in its sole discretion. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.3 Acra requires all individuals with direct or indirect ownership ≥ 20% to provide a recourse guarantee (Acra approved, or Exhibit 7) in the case of an entity borrower. All recourse is joint and several in the case of multiple guarantors. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.4 An entity borrower must be a single purpose entity (SPE): “an entity with no assets other than residential investment or rental properties; engaged in the business of owning and operating residential investment or rental properties.” Series limited liability companies are not allowed. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.5 All entities that will hold direct ownership of the subject property and will be on title as a direct owner are required to be a borrowing entity. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.6 Changes to the operating agreement or bylaws with the intent of changing ownership percentages to circumvent required personal guarantors will not be considered. “Lookback to changes cannot occur within 30 days prior to an Application Date or throughout the application process as these changes will not be recognized by Acra Lending.” \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.7 Entity / guarantor types allowed: Domestic Corporations (C and S Corp); single purpose Limited Liability Companies (LLC), excluding series LLC; Limited Liability Partnership (LLP); Limited Liability Limited Partnership (LLLP); General Partnership (GP); Limited Partnership (LP); and Sole Proprietorship. “In all events, the Borrower must be a US formed and based Entity, foreign entities (i.e.: entities formed or based outside the US) or foreign owned entities are not allowed.” \[G §3.12, p. 8\]

condition.purpose: Determine whether the required due diligence is current and the stated Key Principals and Entities are included in background review.
steps: Initial Document Review: Review the loan approval or draw date and the available borrower, guarantor, entity, ownership, and managing-control information.

Eligibility Verification: Identify the Key Principals and Entities in scope: for entity borrowers, the entity, recourse guarantor(s), and any party (individual or entity) that owns 20% or more of the entity directly or indirectly or has managing control; for individual borrowers, all such individuals.

Validation and Verification: Verify borrower / guarantor due diligence is current as of the date of any loan approval or draw, using the schedule referred to by the source. Acra may order background checks on all Key Principals and Entities from Checkpoint, LexisNexis or another comparable provider, including criminal history, OFAC searches, litigation, judgment, and lien searches.
Final Determination: Determine whether the required current due diligence and stated review scope are established; do not infer the omitted schedule.

6.1 Entity eligibility and guarantees
STD-6.1 Business Entities are eligible for financing on business purpose transactions (investment properties exclusively). \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.2 Acra will lend to, and require that title to the collateral be held, either (i) directly by an individual person(s) or (ii) by an entity acceptable to Acra in its sole discretion. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.3 Acra requires all individuals with direct or indirect ownership ≥ 20% to provide a recourse guarantee (Acra approved, or Exhibit 7) in the case of an entity borrower. All recourse is joint and several in the case of multiple guarantors. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.4 An entity borrower must be a single purpose entity (SPE): “an entity with no assets other than residential investment or rental properties; engaged in the business of owning and operating residential investment or rental properties.” Series limited liability companies are not allowed. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.5 All entities that will hold direct ownership of the subject property and will be on title as a direct owner are required to be a borrowing entity. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.6 Changes to the operating agreement or bylaws with the intent of changing ownership percentages to circumvent required personal guarantors will not be considered. “Lookback to changes cannot occur within 30 days prior to an Application Date or throughout the application process as these changes will not be recognized by Acra Lending.” \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.7 Entity / guarantor types allowed: Domestic Corporations (C and S Corp); single purpose Limited Liability Companies (LLC), excluding series LLC; Limited Liability Partnership (LLP); Limited Liability Limited Partnership (LLLP); General Partnership (GP); Limited Partnership (LP); and Sole Proprietorship. “In all events, the Borrower must be a US formed and based Entity, foreign entities (i.e.: entities formed or based outside the US) or foreign owned entities are not allowed.” \[G §3.12, p. 8\]

condition.purpose: Determine whether the required entity documentation is provided without exception and meets the source’s stated requirements.
steps: Initial Document Review: Review the entity documents and compare them with each applicable requirement below. Borrower letters stating that documents are not required, available, or excused from providing such documents are not acceptable.
Eligibility Verification: Verify receipt of a complete, legible Certificate of Formation / Articles of Organization and all amendments thereto.

Validation and Verification: For LLCs and Partnerships, verify a complete (with all referenced exhibits), legible Operating Agreement and all amendments; for corporations, verify Bylaws and all amendments. Verify that the applicable document states whether the entity is member or manager managed, contains authorization to borrow money and enter into contracts for mortgage assets, and designates signers. If formation documents and the Operating Agreement or Bylaws conflict, verify additional information required to address the conflict. Verify documentation evidencing all ownership interests: for LLCs and Partnerships, the Operating Agreement identifies, or attaches as an exhibit, all persons by name with their ownership interest, or copies of membership interest certificates / units in compliance with the Operating Agreement. For S or C Corporations, verify shareholder / stockholder certificates that comply with the Bylaws, if any, or, if stock certificates are lost or unavailable, the corporation’s stock ledger; verify that the certificate or ledger accounts for all outstanding shares noted in the Certificate of Formation / Articles of Organization, including those held by the corporation. If stock certificates are lost, destroyed, mutilated, or otherwise unavailable, verify an Affidavit of Lost Stock Certificate. For S-corporations or Partnerships where both stock certificate and stock ledger are unavailable, verify (i) the most recent preceding tax year’s K-1 statement for all members with 20% or more interest, and (ii) a letter from the CPA or Tax Preparer affirming current ownership interest, with a statement to that effect if the preceding year’s taxes have not been filed.
Final Determination: Determine whether every applicable document requirement is met; do not accept borrower letters as substitutes or exceptions.
checks: A complete, legible Certificate of Formation / Articles of Organization and all amendments thereto is provided.

The applicable complete, legible Operating Agreement or Bylaws, with all amendments and referenced exhibits where required, is provided and contains the stated management, borrowing, contracting, and signer provisions; additional information required to resolve conflicts is provided.
All applicable ownership-interest documentation is provided and meets the stated requirements for LLCs and Partnerships, S or C Corporations, and the stated unavailable-stock-document alternatives.
If stock certificates are lost, destroyed, mutilated, or otherwise unavailable, an Affidavit of Lost Stock Certificate is provided.

If both stock certificate and stock ledger are unavailable for an S-corporation or Partnership, the most recent preceding tax year’s K-1 statement for all members with 20% or more interest and the CPA or Tax Preparer letter affirming current ownership interest are provided, including the stated tax-filing statement where applicable.

condition.purpose: Determine whether title vesting in the trust is permitted under the source’s stated requirements.
steps: Initial Document Review: Review the complete, legible Trust or Certification of Trust and supporting trust, title, and exception documents.

Eligibility Verification: Verify the Trust or Certification states the existence and date of the Trust; Trustor(s) and current Trustee(s); Trustee powers; whether the Trust is revocable and, if revocable, who holds the right to revoke; names and number of Trustees required to sign on behalf of the Trust; Trust identification number (a Social Security number or an IRS-issued Tax Identification Number); how title to Trust assets should be taken; and that the Trust has not been revoked, modified, or amended in any manner. Verify that the Trust is valid under the laws of the state in which it is established; is revocable and can be changed or canceled at any time for any reason during a Trustor’s lifetime; is established by one or more natural persons, solely or jointly (Grantor, Trustor, or Settlor), and becomes effective during their lifetime; and has as its primary beneficiary the individual(s) establishing the Trust.

Validation and Verification: Verify written exception by Acra Senior Management if the Trustor(s) and Trustee(s) are not the same. Verify that the Trust specifies the Trustee has power to hold title and mortgage the property; that the beneficiary does not need to grant written consent for the Trust to borrow money, or that such consent has been granted in writing for purposes of the mortgage; that there is no unusual risk or impairment to the lender’s rights; and that holding title in the Trust does not diminish the lender’s rights as a creditor. Address any additional supporting documentation for which Legal conditions in its sole discretion.
Final Determination: Permit trust vesting only when every applicable stated requirement is met.

ledger.clause:
6.1 Entity eligibility and guarantees
STD-6.1 Business Entities are eligible for financing on business purpose transactions (investment properties exclusively). \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.2 Acra will lend to, and require that title to the collateral be held, either (i) directly by an individual person(s) or (ii) by an entity acceptable to Acra in its sole discretion. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.3 Acra requires all individuals with direct or indirect ownership ≥ 20% to provide a recourse guarantee (Acra approved, or Exhibit 7) in the case of an entity borrower. All recourse is joint and several in the case of multiple guarantors. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.4 An entity borrower must be a single purpose entity (SPE): “an entity with no assets other than residential investment or rental properties; engaged in the business of owning and operating residential investment or rental properties.” Series limited liability companies are not allowed. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.5 All entities that will hold direct ownership of the subject property and will be on title as a direct owner are required to be a borrowing entity. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.6 Changes to the operating agreement or bylaws with the intent of changing ownership percentages to circumvent required personal guarantors will not be considered. “Lookback to changes cannot occur within 30 days prior to an Application Date or throughout the application process as these changes will not be recognized by Acra Lending.” \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.7 Entity / guarantor types allowed: Domestic Corporations (C and S Corp); single purpose Limited Liability Companies (LLC), excluding series LLC; Limited Liability Partnership (LLP); Limited Liability Limited Partnership (LLLP); General Partnership (GP); Limited Partnership (LP); and Sole Proprietorship. “In all events, the Borrower must be a US formed and based Entity, foreign entities (i.e.: entities formed or based outside the US) or foreign owned entities are not allowed.” \[G §3.12, p. 8\]

condition.purpose: Determine whether the mortgage / rental rating is evaluated over the required period and the required property histories are documented.
steps: Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Review credit reports and file documentation for borrower and / or guarantor properties owned or rented over the last twelve (12) months; consider all reported mortgages on credit.

ledger.clause:
7.2 Mortgage / rental rating and payment history
STD-7.6 The mortgage / rental rating for determining mortgage pricing is determined by evaluating the ratings for properties the borrower owns and / or rents over the last twelve (12) months. All reported mortgages on credit should be considered; where the applicant has mortgages that are not reported, the file should contain documentation to evaluate history on the applicant's primary residence(s), any secondary residence(s), and the subject property. \[G §4.15, p. 5\]

STD-7.7 DSCR loans only require documentation on the subject property, principal residence, and second home (if any) of the borrower and / or guarantor(s). Additional properties do not require housing history to be documented unless documents in the file suggest a major credit event has occurred, for example a foreclosure listing the borrower (individually or as guarantor) on the credit report. For DSCR loans, the payment history is required for the primary residence, subject property, and second homes, if applicable. \[G §4.15, p. 5; §6.7, p. 6\]

STD-7.8 Loans that have matured are rated based on the maturity date of the loan; any extensions of the maturity date must be in writing. \[G §4.15, p. 5\]

ledger.clause:
4.1 Citizenship types and limits
STD-4.1 Eligible borrower citizenship types: US Citizen, Permanent Resident, Non-Permanent Resident, Foreign National, ITIN. \[S: Borrower Citizenship\]

STD-4.2 Permanent Resident must have an unexpired PRA ID and SSA card / SSA-89. \[S: Borrower Citizenship\]

STD-4.3 Non-Permanent Resident must have proof of legal residency, which may include an unexpired employment authorization document (EAD) or valid visa. Limit printed as “Max Loan Amount: \$1.5M: Max CLTV 80%” — whether this is two independent limits or one conditional limit: Acra confirmation requested → Q-21. \[S: Borrower Citizenship\]

STD-4.4 Foreign National: “Borrowers whose Primary Residence is not located in the United States of America.” Maximum CLTV 70% (purchase) and 65% (refinance — rate & term and cash-out); “Price loan at FICO equal to 700”. No maximum loan amount is stated for foreign nationals: Acra confirmation requested → Q-21. Program documentation is in section 5. \[S: Borrower Citizenship\]

STD-4.5 ITIN: “ITIN is defined as any non-resident that is unable to provide any of the ‘Non-Permanent Resident Alien’ documents listed above.” Maximum loan amount \$1.0M; minimum FICO 640; maximum CLTV by FICO as printed below. §3.10 separately admits ITIN holders under the foreign-national program when they reside outside the US. Whether a US-resident ITIN holder is eligible, and whether the tier printed “FICO 700” means 700 and above: Acra confirmation requested → Q-03. \[S: Borrower Citizenship; G §3.10, p. 6\]

| **ITIN tier as printed** | **Purchase** | **Refinance — R/T and cash-out** |
|--------------------------|--------------|----------------------------------|
| “FICO 700”               | 70%          | 65%                              |
| “FICO 660 to 699”        | 65%          | 60%                              |
| “FICO 640 to 659”        | 60%          | 60%                              |

STD-5.1 Foreign Nationals are eligible for financing on business purpose transactions only (i.e. investment properties). \[G §3.10, p. 6\]

STD-5.2 Eligible under the Foreign National Program are Non-Resident Aliens who are not authorized to live or work in the U.S. “A true Foreign National may periodically visit the U.S. for various reasons including vacation and / or business, may purchase property for limited personal use or investment, or may own a U.S based business entity, but they must reside outside of the U.S.” \[G §3.10, p. 6\]

STD-5.3 Borrowers who are holders of Individual Tax Identification Numbers (ITIN) are eligible for this program if they reside outside of the U.S. \[G §3.10, p. 6\]

STD-5.5 “See 3.10 for OFAC restrictions and state specific exclusions” — not reproduced (Appendix B). \[G §3.10, p. 7\]

Eligibility Verification: Determine whether at least one listed alternative is provided: (1) a U.S. credit report with at least two (2) trade lines with minimum age of two (2) years for one trade line; (2) an international credit report; (3) an original credit reference letter from an internationally known financial institution; or (4) a bank statement documenting a foreign financial banking relationship for the past 60 days.
Validation and Verification: Verify the selected alternative. The original letter need not include details or payment histories of debt obligations located outside of the U.S.
Final Determination: Record which alternative, if any, meets its stated terms.

4.1 Citizenship types and limits
STD-4.1 Eligible borrower citizenship types: US Citizen, Permanent Resident, Non-Permanent Resident, Foreign National, ITIN. \[S: Borrower Citizenship\]

STD-4.2 Permanent Resident must have an unexpired PRA ID and SSA card / SSA-89. \[S: Borrower Citizenship\]

STD-4.3 Non-Permanent Resident must have proof of legal residency, which may include an unexpired employment authorization document (EAD) or valid visa. STD-5.1 Foreign Nationals are eligible for financing on business purpose transactions only (i.e. investment properties). \[G §3.10, p. 6\]

STD-5.2 Eligible under the Foreign National Program are Non-Resident Aliens who are not authorized to live or work in the U.S. “A true Foreign National may periodically visit the U.S. for various reasons including vacation and / or business, may purchase property for limited personal use or investment, or may own a U.S based business entity, but they must reside outside of the U.S.” \[G §3.10, p. 6\]

STD-5.5 “See 3.10 for OFAC restrictions and state specific exclusions” — not reproduced (Appendix B). \[G §3.10, p. 7\]

condition.purpose: Determine whether an outside-U.S.-signed document meets one of the acknowledgment routes stated in the guideline and is acceptable to the title company.
steps: Initial Document Review: Identify documents signed outside of the U.S., the signing country, and the submitted acknowledgment and authentication materials.

Eligibility Verification: Determine which stated route applies: U.S. embassy or consular official notarization; or, for a country party to the Hague Convention Treaty Abolishing the Requirement of Legalization for Foreign Public Documents, authorized notary public acknowledgment plus English apostille attached to the executed documents.

Validation and Verification: For the embassy or consular route, verify the certificate of acknowledgement includes the embassy or consular seal and is acceptable to the title company. For the Hague Convention route, verify the certificate is completed and signed by an authorized notary public, authentication by apostille is in English and attached to the executed documents, and the title company accepts it.
Final Determination: Record whether the applicable route and title company acceptance are verified.
checks: Each document signed outside of the U.S. has an applicable stated acknowledgment route: embassy or consular notarization with seal and title company acceptance, or, for a party country under the stated Hague Convention Treaty, authorized notary acknowledgment with English apostille attached to the executed documents and title company acceptance.

ledger.clause:
4.1 Citizenship types and limits
STD-4.1 Eligible borrower citizenship types: US Citizen, Permanent Resident, Non-Permanent Resident, Foreign National, ITIN. \[S: Borrower Citizenship\]

STD-4.2 Permanent Resident must have an unexpired PRA ID and SSA card / SSA-89. \[S: Borrower Citizenship\]

STD-4.3 Non-Permanent Resident must have proof of legal residency, which may include an unexpired employment authorization document (EAD) or valid visa. Limit printed as “Max Loan Amount: \$1.5M: Max CLTV 80%” — whether this is two independent limits or one conditional limit: Acra confirmation requested → Q-21. \[S: Borrower Citizenship\]

STD-4.4 Foreign National: “Borrowers whose Primary Residence is not located in the United States of America.” Maximum CLTV 70% (purchase) and 65% (refinance — rate & term and cash-out); “Price loan at FICO equal to 700”. No maximum loan amount is stated for foreign nationals: Acra confirmation requested → Q-21. Program documentation is in section 5. \[S: Borrower Citizenship\]

STD-4.5 ITIN: “ITIN is defined as any non-resident that is unable to provide any of the ‘Non-Permanent Resident Alien’ documents listed above.” Maximum loan amount \$1.0M; minimum FICO 640; maximum CLTV by FICO as printed below. §3.10 separately admits ITIN holders under the foreign-national program when they reside outside the US. Whether a US-resident ITIN holder is eligible, and whether the tier printed “FICO 700” means 700 and above: Acra confirmation requested → Q-03. \[S: Borrower Citizenship; G §3.10, p. 6\]

| **ITIN tier as printed** | **Purchase** | **Refinance — R/T and cash-out** |
|--------------------------|--------------|----------------------------------|
| “FICO 700”               | 70%          | 65%                              |
| “FICO 660 to 699”        | 65%          | 60%                              |
| “FICO 640 to 659”        | 60%          | 60%                              |

condition.purpose: Resolve the source's stated uncertainty about whether “Max Loan Amount: $1.5M: Max CLTV 80%” means two independent limits or one conditional limit.

Final Determination: Record the confirmed interpretation for application of the limits.
checks: For a Non-Permanent Resident, Acra has confirmed whether “Max Loan Amount: $1.5M: Max CLTV 80%” means two independent limits or one conditional limit.

condition.purpose: Verify the required 1007 rent schedule for applicable DSCR files and transactions.
steps: Initial Document Review: Review the appraisal report and identify property type, DSCR qualification method, and whether proposed rental income is being used to qualify.

Eligibility Verification: A 1007 is required on DSCR transactions, including No Ratio DSCR. For single family properties, apply the stated 1007 requirements for DSCR qualifying files, lease-option purchases where the down payment required in §3.45 is generated from excess monthly rent contributions, and proposed rental income used to qualify.

Validation and Verification: Verify that the 1007 is from the original appraiser or any state licensed appraiser. If considering a Form 1025 as satisfying the 1007 requirement for a 2-4 unit property, obtain Acra confirmation; the source leaves this unresolved.
Final Determination: Record compliance with applicable 1007 requirements and any pending Acra confirmation.

The 1007 is from the original appraiser or any state licensed appraiser.
Use of Form 1025 to satisfy the 1007 requirement for a 2-4 unit property is referred for Acra confirmation.

ledger.clause:
1.1 Occupancy, purpose and qualification
STD-1.7 “A 1007 will always be required on DSCR transactions – for avoidance of doubt, even on No Ratio DSCR”. Whether a Form 1025 satisfies this for a 2-4 unit property: Acra confirmation requested → Q-08. \[G §5.32, p. 3; §14.12, p. 4\]

STD-1.8 All borrowers purchasing or refinancing a one- to four-family investment property must execute a One- to Four-Family Rider with the loan documents and provide rent loss insurance coverage per §23.40 (STD-8.11 to 8.14). \[G §3.41, p. 11\]

STD-1.9 Only the subject property, principal residence and second homes are required to be listed on the application or Schedule of Real Estate Owned. \[G §5.32, p. 3; §4.15, p. 5\]

3.3 Rent schedules and rent evidence
STD-3.9 Acra requires the Single-Family Comparable Rent Schedule (FNMA Form 1007) for single family properties on (i) all DSCR qualifying files, (ii) lease-option purchase transactions where the down payment required in §3.45 is generated from excess monthly rent contributions, or (iii) when proposed rental income is being used to qualify. \[G §14.12, p. 4\]

STD-3.10 A 1007 may be from the original appraiser or any state licensed appraiser. \[G §14.12, p. 4\]

STD-3.11 Single family investment properties with excessive monthly rent payments reflected on the lease require documentation supporting that the monthly rent is typical for the area; acceptable documentation may include classified ads from local newspapers, a 1007 completed by the appraiser, or a market rent survey completed by a local real estate company or rental management company familiar with the market rents in the area. \[G §14.12, p. 4\]

STD-3.12 Short-term rental, appraisal form: for properties occupied as a short-term rental, an STRpro or similar appraisal form is acceptable as replacement to a 1007 as long as it is signed by an appropriately licensed appraiser. \[G §14.13, p. 4\]

STD-3.13 Short-term rental, actual rents: “Acra can accept short term rentals with 12-month ledgers from condotel management companies, property managers, AirBnB, VRBO, etcetera as documentation for actual rents.” How a 12-month ledger establishes qualifying rent, and how the receipt and lease conditions of STD-3.6 apply to short-term rentals: Acra confirmation requested → Q-02. \[G §5.32, p. 3; §14.13, p. 4\]

STD-3.14 Short-term rental caps: “Properties qualifying with short-term rentals are limited to 75% & 70% LTV / CLTV for Purchase or Refinance transactions respectively”; the Summary states maximum CLTV 75% (purchase) and 70% (refinance — rate & term and cash-out), minimum FICO 640. \[G §5.32, p. 3; S: Occupancy Type\]

3.5 No Ratio DSCR
STD-3.19 “File can qualify without calculating a DSCR Ratio to a maximum LTV / CLTV as described on the appropriate program matrix depending on FICO and other requirement. Requires 1007; however, DSCR is not calculated.” The Summary's No Ratio caps and minimum FICO are STD-3.17. \[G §5.33, p. 3; S: Income Documentation\]

STD-3.20 “Proof of actual rents is not required. Property may be short-term rental or long-term rental (appropriate pricing applies).” \[G §5.33, p. 3\]

STD-3.21 Whether No Ratio is available where another condition carries its own minimum DSCR (STD-3.16 and the table above): Acra confirmation requested → Q-13. Whether the short-term-rental caps apply to a No Ratio file: Acra confirmation requested → Q-02.

STD-3.22 Rent loss insurance applies to No Ratio DSCR (STD-8.12). \[G §23.40, p. 13\]

ledger.clause:
3.1 The ratio
STD-3.1 “Acra calculates the DSCR by dividing (a) the lesser of (i) annual in-place rent or (ii) market rent (reference §14.14) by (b) the sum of annual principal, interest, real estate taxes, property insurance, and homeowner's / condominium association fees (collectively, ‘PITIA’). Subordinate financing, if applicable, would also be included in the denominator for the sake of this calculation.” \[G §5.32, p. 3\]

STD-3.2 “Acra calculates the DSCR utilizing the first payment due under the terms of the Note.” §7.5 defines Interest Only payments as “the amount sufficient to pay the accrued interest to the mortgage on a monthly basis at the time of origination”, while the §5.32 denominator lists “annual principal, interest …”. 3.3 Rent schedules and rent evidence
STD-3.9 Acra requires the Single-Family Comparable Rent Schedule (FNMA Form 1007) for single family properties on (i) all DSCR qualifying files, (ii) lease-option purchase transactions where the down payment required in §3.45 is generated from excess monthly rent contributions, or (iii) when proposed rental income is being used to qualify. \[G §14.12, p. 4\]

STD-3.10 A 1007 may be from the original appraiser or any state licensed appraiser. \[G §14.12, p. 4\]

STD-3.11 Single family investment properties with excessive monthly rent payments reflected on the lease require documentation supporting that the monthly rent is typical for the area; acceptable documentation may include classified ads from local newspapers, a 1007 completed by the appraiser, or a market rent survey completed by a local real estate company or rental management company familiar with the market rents in the area. \[G §14.12, p. 4\]

STD-3.12 Short-term rental, appraisal form: for properties occupied as a short-term rental, an STRpro or similar appraisal form is acceptable as replacement to a 1007 as long as it is signed by an appropriately licensed appraiser. \[G §14.13, p. 4\]

STD-3.13 Short-term rental, actual rents: “Acra can accept short term rentals with 12-month ledgers from condotel management companies, property managers, AirBnB, VRBO, etcetera as documentation for actual rents.” How a 12-month ledger establishes qualifying rent, and how the receipt and lease conditions of STD-3.6 apply to short-term rentals: Acra confirmation requested → Q-02. \[G §5.32, p. 3; §14.13, p. 4\]

STD-3.14 Short-term rental caps: “Properties qualifying with short-term rentals are limited to 75% & 70% LTV / CLTV for Purchase or Refinance transactions respectively”; the Summary states maximum CLTV 75% (purchase) and 70% (refinance — rate & term and cash-out), minimum FICO 640. \[G §5.32, p. 3; S: Occupancy Type\]

condition.purpose: Determine whether the stated No Ratio rules are applied without calculating a DSCR.
steps: Initial Document Review: Review the application, 1007, and rent evidence.
Eligibility Verification: Determine whether the file qualifies as No Ratio DSCR under the appropriate program matrix depending on FICO and other requirement.

Validation and Verification: Do not calculate DSCR. Verify a 1007 is provided. Proof of actual rents is not required; property may be short-term rental or long-term rental (appropriate pricing applies). Refer to Acra confirmation whether No Ratio is available where another condition carries its own minimum DSCR and whether short-term-rental caps apply to a No Ratio file.
Final Determination: Record No Ratio treatment and any pending confirmation.
checks: For No Ratio DSCR, DSCR is not calculated.
A 1007 is provided for No Ratio DSCR.
Proof of actual rents is not required for No Ratio DSCR.
No Ratio DSCR is referred for Acra confirmation when another condition carries its own minimum DSCR.
Whether short-term-rental caps apply to a No Ratio file is referred for Acra confirmation.

outcomes.criterion: No Ratio treatment is applied as stated, and the unresolved applicability questions are referred for confirmation.

3.5 No Ratio DSCR
STD-3.19 “File can qualify without calculating a DSCR Ratio to a maximum LTV / CLTV as described on the appropriate program matrix depending on FICO and other requirement. Requires 1007; however, DSCR is not calculated.” The Summary's No Ratio caps and minimum FICO are STD-3.17. \[G §5.33, p. 3; S: Income Documentation\]

STD-3.20 “Proof of actual rents is not required. Property may be short-term rental or long-term rental (appropriate pricing applies).” \[G §5.33, p. 3\]

STD-3.21 Whether No Ratio is available where another condition carries its own minimum DSCR (STD-3.16 and the table above): Acra confirmation requested → Q-13. Whether the short-term-rental caps apply to a No Ratio file: Acra confirmation requested → Q-02.

STD-3.22 Rent loss insurance applies to No Ratio DSCR (STD-8.12). \[G §23.40, p. 13\]

1.1 Occupancy, purpose and qualification
STD-1.7 “A 1007 will always be required on DSCR transactions – for avoidance of doubt, even on No Ratio DSCR”. Whether a Form 1025 satisfies this for a 2-4 unit property: Acra confirmation requested → Q-08. \[G §5.32, p. 3; §14.12, p. 4\]

STD-1.8 All borrowers purchasing or refinancing a one- to four-family investment property must execute a One- to Four-Family Rider with the loan documents and provide rent loss insurance coverage per §23.40 (STD-8.11 to 8.14). \[G §3.41, p. 11\]

STD-1.9 Only the subject property, principal residence and second homes are required to be listed on the application or Schedule of Real Estate Owned. \[G §5.32, p. 3; §4.15, p. 5\]

3.3 Rent schedules and rent evidence
STD-3.9 Acra requires the Single-Family Comparable Rent Schedule (FNMA Form 1007) for single family properties on (i) all DSCR qualifying files, (ii) lease-option purchase transactions where the down payment required in §3.45 is generated from excess monthly rent contributions, or (iii) when proposed rental income is being used to qualify. \[G §14.12, p. 4\]

STD-3.10 A 1007 may be from the original appraiser or any state licensed appraiser. \[G §14.12, p. 4\]

STD-3.11 Single family investment properties with excessive monthly rent payments reflected on the lease require documentation supporting that the monthly rent is typical for the area; acceptable documentation may include classified ads from local newspapers, a 1007 completed by the appraiser, or a market rent survey completed by a local real estate company or rental management company familiar with the market rents in the area. \[G §14.12, p. 4\]

STD-3.12 Short-term rental, appraisal form: for properties occupied as a short-term rental, an STRpro or similar appraisal form is acceptable as replacement to a 1007 as long as it is signed by an appropriately licensed appraiser. \[G §14.13, p. 4\]

STD-3.13 Short-term rental, actual rents: “Acra can accept short term rentals with 12-month ledgers from condotel management companies, property managers, AirBnB, VRBO, etcetera as documentation for actual rents.” How a 12-month ledger establishes qualifying rent, and how the receipt and lease conditions of STD-3.6 apply to short-term rentals: Acra confirmation requested → Q-02. \[G §5.32, p. 3; §14.13, p. 4\]

STD-3.14 Short-term rental caps: “Properties qualifying with short-term rentals are limited to 75% & 70% LTV / CLTV for Purchase or Refinance transactions respectively”; the Summary states maximum CLTV 75% (purchase) and 70% (refinance — rate & term and cash-out), minimum FICO 640. \[G §5.32, p. 3; S: Occupancy Type\]

condition.purpose: Evaluate the rent evidence without resolving the source's conflicting instructions on which rent may qualify.
steps: Initial Document Review: Review the lease agreement, evidence of actual rent receipt, and market-rent evidence.
Eligibility Verification: Determine whether actual rent exceeds market rent.

Validation and Verification: If actual rent exceeds market rent, verify evidence of two (2) consecutive months proof of rental income receipt and lease agreement(s) to continue at a minimum of three (3) months after closing. Do not count a Security Deposit as receipt; rents cannot be prepaid. Do not choose between the conflicting rent formulations in the source; refer the issue for Acra confirmation.
Final Determination: Record the rent evidence and whether the stated documentation conditions are met; leave the qualifying-rent choice subject to Acra confirmation.
checks: The rent basis used for qualification is not selected without Acra confirmation where the source's two formulations conflict.
Where actual rents exceed market rents and actual-rent evidence is relied upon, two (2) consecutive months proof of rental income receipt is documented.
Where actual rents exceed market rents and actual-rent evidence is relied upon, lease agreement(s) continue at a minimum of three (3) months after closing.
A Security Deposit is not counted as receipt, and rents are not prepaid.

outcomes.criterion: Applicable stated actual-rent documentation conditions are met, and the unresolved rent-basis question is referred for confirmation.

ledger.clause:
3.3 Rent schedules and rent evidence
STD-3.9 Acra requires the Single-Family Comparable Rent Schedule (FNMA Form 1007) for single family properties on (i) all DSCR qualifying files, (ii) lease-option purchase transactions where the down payment required in §3.45 is generated from excess monthly rent contributions, or (iii) when proposed rental income is being used to qualify. \[G §14.12, p. 4\]

STD-3.10 A 1007 may be from the original appraiser or any state licensed appraiser. \[G §14.12, p. 4\]

STD-3.11 Single family investment properties with excessive monthly rent payments reflected on the lease require documentation supporting that the monthly rent is typical for the area; acceptable documentation may include classified ads from local newspapers, a 1007 completed by the appraiser, or a market rent survey completed by a local real estate company or rental management company familiar with the market rents in the area. \[G §14.12, p. 4\]

STD-3.12 Short-term rental, appraisal form: for properties occupied as a short-term rental, an STRpro or similar appraisal form is acceptable as replacement to a 1007 as long as it is signed by an appropriately licensed appraiser. \[G §14.13, p. 4\]

STD-3.13 Short-term rental, actual rents: “Acra can accept short term rentals with 12-month ledgers from condotel management companies, property managers, AirBnB, VRBO, etcetera as documentation for actual rents.” How a 12-month ledger establishes qualifying rent, and how the receipt and lease conditions of STD-3.6 apply to short-term rentals: Acra confirmation requested → Q-02. \[G §5.32, p. 3; §14.13, p. 4\]

STD-3.14 Short-term rental caps: “Properties qualifying with short-term rentals are limited to 75% & 70% LTV / CLTV for Purchase or Refinance transactions respectively”; the Summary states maximum CLTV 75% (purchase) and 70% (refinance — rate & term and cash-out), minimum FICO 640. \[G §5.32, p. 3; S: Occupancy Type\]

1.1 Occupancy, purpose and qualification
STD-1.1 Occupancy is investment property (non-owner occupied) only. \[S: Occupancy Type\]

STD-1.2 An investment property is “a one- to four-unit residential dwelling or a unit in a condominium complex or a PUD owned by an individual who does not occupy the dwelling. The dwelling is leased and occupied as a principal year-round residence to individuals other than the owner.” \[G §3.41, p. 11\]

STD-1.3 The Program Summary is listed as “Business Purpose DSCR” on Acra's rate-sheet page. “Where the borrower is qualifying utilizing the subject property's actual or market cashflow under a business purpose transaction, borrower must execute with loan docs a Business Purpose Attestation (Exhibit 8) or other similar attestation approved by Acra.” The excerpt's §8.4 also refers to consumer transactions (STD-9.2); whether every loan on this program is a business-purpose transaction: Acra confirmation requested → Q-27. \[G §5.32, p. 3; acralending.com/ratesheets\]

STD-1.4 The matrix columns are Purchase, Rate & Term and Cash-Out. Delayed financing is addressed only by the matrix footnote “Delayed financing is capped at \$1.5MM”. Which column and which cash-in-hand rule apply to delayed financing: Acra confirmation requested → Q-06. \[S: matrix and footnote\]

STD-1.5 A loan qualifies either by a calculated DSCR (§5.32) or as No Ratio DSCR, where no ratio is calculated (§5.33). Both are set out in section 3. \[G §5.32–5.33, p. 3\]

STD-1.6 “Borrowing entity income documentation not required.” Acra will not calculate a DTI for applicants who qualify using a DSCR; income or employment listed on an application is superfluous to the underwrite and may be left blank, and if represented, a DTI should not be calculated. \[S: Income Documentation; G §7.3, p. 5\]

condition.purpose: Determine whether the loan meets the applicable matrix FICO and CLTV limits.
steps: Initial Document Review: Review the loan_application and credit_report for loan amount, transaction type, FICO score, and CLTV.
Eligibility Verification: Select the printed loan-amount tier and the applicable minimum-FICO row; use the Purchase, Rate & Term, or Cash-Out column.
Validation and Verification: Compare the loan's CLTV to the matrix maximum. Treat NA as printed and do not assign a matrix value below 600 for loans of $1,500,000 or less.
Final Determination: Record whether the applicable matrix FICO and CLTV requirements are met.
checks: For loans ≤ $1,500,000, FICO is at least 600 and CLTV does not exceed the printed matrix maximum for the applicable FICO row and transaction type.
For loans $1,500,001–$2,000,000, FICO is at least 620 and the applicable transaction-type cell is not NA, and CLTV does not exceed its printed maximum.
For loans $2,000,001–$3,000,000, FICO is at least 700 and CLTV does not exceed the printed matrix maximum for the applicable transaction type.
For loans of $1,500,000 or less with FICO below 600, record that the matrix has no published value; do not treat this source text as a determination of ineligibility.

outcomes.criterion: Every applicable matrix requirement is met.
There is no case for this outcome.
An applicable published matrix requirement is not met, including an applicable NA cell.
The case is not a loan request under the Investment Property matrix.

missing_reads: The source does not state whether loans of $1,500,000 or less with FICO below 600 are ineligible (Q-16).

ledger.clause:
4.3 First-time homebuyers
STD-4.9 “Acra defines a First Time Home Buyers (‘FTHB’) as an application where all Applicants have never previously owned a home (real property).” \[G §3.13, p. 10\]

STD-4.10 DSCR: Acra allows first-time homebuyers under all of the following: minimum 700 FICO score; maximum 70% CLTV; minimum DSCR of 1.150; maximum loan amount of \$1,000,000; full amortization required, no interest-only programs; impounds required; minimum six months reserves. The Summary states the same conditions: “Minimum 700 FICO: Max 70% CLTV: DSCR ≥ 1.15: Loan amt ≤ \$1MM: NO I/O: Must Impound: Requires 6mos Reserves”. \[G §3.13, p. 10; S: Restrictions\]

STD-4.11 “Where a FTHB is purchasing an Investment property and the loan is qualifying via DTI program, the maximum DTI will be 43.0%.” Noted as a DTI-program provision — Q-14. \[G §3.13, p. 10\]

STD-4.12 §3.12 separately requires at least one guarantor with prior homeownership experience where the borrower is an entity (STD-6.9). How that requirement and the first-time-homebuyer allowance interact: Acra confirmation requested → Q-09.

STD-1.2 An investment property is “a one- to four-unit residential dwelling or a unit in a condominium complex or a PUD owned by an individual who does not occupy the dwelling. The dwelling is leased and occupied as a principal year-round residence to individuals other than the owner.” \[G §3.41, p. 11\]

STD-1.3 The Program Summary is listed as “Business Purpose DSCR” on Acra's rate-sheet page. “Where the borrower is qualifying utilizing the subject property's actual or market cashflow under a business purpose transaction, borrower must execute with loan docs a Business Purpose Attestation (Exhibit 8) or other similar attestation approved by Acra.” The excerpt's §8.4 also refers to consumer transactions (STD-9.2); whether every loan on this program is a business-purpose transaction: Acra confirmation requested → Q-27. \[G §5.32, p. 3; acralending.com/ratesheets\]

STD-1.4 The matrix columns are Purchase, Rate & Term and Cash-Out. Delayed financing is addressed only by the matrix footnote “Delayed financing is capped at \$1.5MM”. Which column and which cash-in-hand rule apply to delayed financing: Acra confirmation requested → Q-06. \[S: matrix and footnote\]

STD-1.5 A loan qualifies either by a calculated DSCR (§5.32) or as No Ratio DSCR, where no ratio is calculated (§5.33). Both are set out in section 3. \[G §5.32–5.33, p. 3\]

STD-1.6 “Borrowing entity income documentation not required.” Acra will not calculate a DTI for applicants who qualify using a DSCR; income or employment listed on an application is superfluous to the underwrite and may be left blank, and if represented, a DTI should not be calculated. \[S: Income Documentation; G §7.3, p. 5\]

condition.purpose: Determine whether the requested loan amount meets the program's stated amount requirements.
steps: Initial Document Review: Review the loan_application for the requested loan amount and product.
Eligibility Verification: Verify that the loan amount is $100,000 to $3,000,000 and is in $50 increments.

Validation and Verification: Apply the stated amount-specific limits: loan amount < $200,000 has maximum CLTV 80% (purchase) and 75% (refinance); loan amount > $2,000,000 must have 1.0 or greater DSCR; delayed financing is capped at $1.5MM; interest-only loans have minimum loan amount $250,000 and maximum loan amount $3,000,000.
Final Determination: Record whether each applicable loan-amount requirement is met; do not resolve the source's open questions about delayed-financing column or cash-in-hand treatment.
checks: The loan amount is $100,000 to $3,000,000.
The loan amount is in $50 increments.
For a loan amount < $200,000, CLTV does not exceed 80% for purchase or 75% for refinance.
For a loan amount > $2,000,000, DSCR is 1.0 or greater.
For delayed financing, the loan amount does not exceed $1.5MM.
For an interest-only loan, the loan amount is at least $250,000 and no more than $3,000,000.

condition.purpose: Determine whether the selected product and its stated terms meet the program requirements.
steps: Initial Document Review: Review the loan_application for product type, loan amount, FICO, ARM terms, property status, and first-time-homebuyer status.

Eligibility Verification: Verify that the product is 30 Yr Fixed; 5/1 ARM; 7/1 ARM; Interest Only (5 Yr / 30 year term, available on 5/1 or 7/1 ARM); Interest Only (5 Yr / 30 Year Fixed); or Interest Only (10 Yr / 40 Year Term).

Validation and Verification: For ARM products, verify Index 1 Yr CMT, Caps 2/2/6, and the margin applicable to FICO: 3.00 (FICO 760+), 3.25 (FICO 720-759), 3.50 (FICO 700-719), 3.75 (FICO 680-699), 4.00 (FICO 660-679), 4.25 (FICO 640-659), or 5.00 (FICO 600-639). For interest-only, verify the applicable $250K minimum, 640 minimum credit score, and, for 10 Yr / 40 Year Term, 80% maximum LTV / CLTV and $3M maximum loan amount. Verify interest-only is not used for a first-time homebuyer, vacant-property refinance, or property listed for sale.
Final Determination: Record whether every applicable product and term requirement is met.
checks: The selected product is one of the eligible product types printed in STD-10.1.

For an interest-only loan, loan amount is at least $250K and FICO is at least 640.
For Interest Only (10 Yr / 40 Year Term), LTV / CLTV does not exceed 80% and loan amount does not exceed $3M.
Interest-only is not used for a first-time homebuyer.
Interest-only is not used on a vacant-property refinance.

10.1 Eligible products and ARM terms
STD-10.1 Eligible product types: 30 Yr Fixed; 5/1 ARM; 7/1 ARM; Interest Only (5 Yr / 30 year term, available on 5/1 or 7/1 ARM); Interest Only (5 Yr / 30 Year Fixed); Interest Only (10 Yr / 40 Year Term). \[S: Product Requirements\]

STD-10.2 ARM requirements: Index 1 Yr CMT; Caps 2/2/6; Margin 3.00 (FICO 760+), 3.25 (FICO 720-759), 3.50 (FICO 700-719), 3.75 (FICO 680-699), 4.00 (FICO 660-679), 4.25 (FICO 640-659), 5.00 (FICO 600-639). \[S: Product Requirements\]

10.2 Interest-only
STD-10.3 Interest Only, 5 Yr / 30 Year Fixed or 5/1 and 7/1 ARM: minimum loan ≥ \$250K; minimum 640 credit score. \[S: Product Requirements\]

STD-10.4 Interest Only, 10 Yr / 40 Year Term: minimum loan ≥ \$250K; minimum 640 credit score; maximum 80% LTV / CLTV; maximum \$3M loan amount. \[S: Product Requirements\]

Acra calculates the DSCR using the first payment due under the Note (STD-3.2; which payment enters the denominator on an interest-only loan is Q-26). The excerpt's DTI calculation for interest-only loans (first fully amortized payment on the original balance; for an ARM, the highest achievable rate at that payment's due date) is a DTI-program provision — Q-14. \[G §7.5, p. 13\]

condition.purpose: Compare CLTV with each published feature-specific cap or adjustment that applies to the case.
steps: Initial Document Review: Review the loan_application, credit_report, and relevant property or project information for the features listed in the published CLTV tables.

Eligibility Verification: Identify which printed feature rows apply, including the matrix tiers, loan amount < $200,000, DSCR < 1.0 or No Ratio, short-term rental, citizenship category, ITIN, score/tradeline status, mortgage history, credit events, property type/status, first-time homebuyer, escrow waiver, and Interest Only 10 Yr / 40 Year Term.

Validation and Verification: Compare CLTV to the applicable published transaction cap and apply a printed −5% adjustment for declining market or Florida Non-Warrantable Condo, Condotel / PUDtel when applicable. Use the published row values as printed.
Final Determination: Record whether the applicable published caps and adjustments are met; do not infer requirements absent from the supplied text.
checks: CLTV does not exceed the applicable published cap for every applicable row in U70 and U71.
For a declining market, the published adjustment of −5% is applied to Purchase, Rate & Term, and Cash-Out.
For Florida Non-Warrantable Condo, Condotel / PUDtel, the published adjustment of −5% is applied to Purchase, Rate & Term, and Cash-Out.
Where a feature has a published minimum FICO in U72, the FICO meets that minimum; Foreign National is priced at FICO 700 and has no minimum stated.

outcomes.criterion: Every applicable published cap, adjustment, and minimum-FICO check holds.
There is no case for this outcome.
An applicable published cap, adjustment, or minimum-FICO check does not hold.
No feature with a published CLTV cap, adjustment, or minimum-FICO requirement applies.

ledger.clause:
7.3 Properties listed for sale (§11.5)
PLAT-7.6 A property is considered listed for sale under §11.5 if it has been listed for sale in the last six months, measured from (a) the last date of being listed to (b) the Application Date. \[G §11.5, p. 12\]

PLAT-7.7 Whether §11.5 applies to Platinum Select unchanged is part of Q-13; it is restated here because the Platinum Summary does not exclude it. \[G §11.5\]

PLAT-7.8 Loans on such properties will be considered under the following characteristics: the property is not in default or otherwise delinquent on lien(s); for investment properties, the subject must be occupied by a tenant and may not be vacant; the loan must qualify as either (a) ≥ 1.0 DSCR or (b) 43% maximum DTI — on this program the channel minimum DSCR applies, Wholesale 1.0 and Correspondent 1.2 (PLAT-3.8), and the DTI alternative is Q-14; a prepayment penalty of at least three (3) years is required unless the property is in a state that does not allow prepayment penalties; twenty-four (24) months of reserves are required, and cash-in-hand may be considered if otherwise consistent with the Guide; the loan must have a fully amortizing term, interest only is not available; the maximum LTV / CLTV is 65% based on the lesser of (a) appraised value or (b) lowest recent listing price; no subordinate financing is allowed; impounds are required. \[G §11.5, pp. 11–12\]

PLAT-7.6 A property is considered listed for sale under §11.5 if it has been listed for sale in the last six months, measured from (a) the last date of being listed to (b) the Application Date. \[G §11.5, p. 12\]

PLAT-7.7 Whether §11.5 applies to Platinum Select unchanged is part of Q-13; it is restated here because the Platinum Summary does not exclude it. \[G §11.5\]

PLAT-7.8 Loans on such properties will be considered under the following characteristics: the property is not in default or otherwise delinquent on lien(s); for investment properties, the subject must be occupied by a tenant and may not be vacant; the loan must qualify as either (a) ≥ 1.0 DSCR or (b) 43% maximum DTI — on this program the channel minimum DSCR applies, Wholesale 1.0 and Correspondent 1.2 (PLAT-3.8), and the DTI alternative is Q-14; a prepayment penalty of at least three (3) years is required unless the property is in a state that does not allow prepayment penalties; twenty-four (24) months of reserves are required, and cash-in-hand may be considered if otherwise consistent with the Guide; the loan must have a fully amortizing term, interest only is not available; the maximum LTV / CLTV is 65% based on the lesser of (a) appraised value or (b) lowest recent listing price; no subordinate financing is allowed; impounds are required. \[G §11.5, pp. 11–12\]

condition.purpose: Check the stated qualification alternatives and the channel minimum DSCR for this program.
steps: Initial Document Review: Review the loan file for channel and DSCR information.
Eligibility Verification: Establish that the property is subject to the §11.5 listed-property characteristics.

Validation and Verification: Check qualification by DSCR at ≥ 1.0, using the channel minimum DSCR applicable on this program: Wholesale 1.0 and Correspondent 1.2. If qualification is by the 43% maximum DTI alternative, obtain resolution of Q-14.
Final Determination: Record whether a stated qualification route is established or the DTI alternative remains unresolved.
checks: The loan qualifies by DSCR at ≥ 1.0 and meets the channel minimum DSCR, or the DTI alternative is resolved in Q-14.

Qualification relies on the 43% maximum DTI alternative and Q-14 has not resolved that alternative.
Neither stated qualification route is established.
The property is not subject to the §11.5 listed-property characteristics.

7.2 Vacant properties
PLAT-7.5 Vacant properties are ineligible (PLAT-1.6). The §10.17 vacant-refinance provisions and the §5.32 rule for qualifying rent on a vacant purchase are not restated (Appendix B). \[P: Loan Purpose Requirements\]

1.1 Occupancy, purpose and qualification
PLAT-1.1 Occupancy: Non-Owner Occupied. \[P: Occupancy Requirements\]

PLAT-1.2 An investment property is “a one- to four-unit residential dwelling or a unit in a condominium complex or a PUD owned by an individual who does not occupy the dwelling. The dwelling is leased and occupied as a principal year-round residence to individuals other than the owner.” The property types the Platinum Summary lists as eligible are at PLAT-7.1; types it does not list are set out in the table at 7.1 and asked in Q-07. \[G §3.41, p. 11; P: Subject Property Requirements\]

PLAT-1.3 The Program Summary is listed as “Business Purpose DSCR Platinum” on Acra's rate-sheet page. “Where the borrower is qualifying utilizing the subject property's actual or market cashflow under a business purpose transaction, borrower must execute with loan docs a Business Purpose Attestation (Exhibit 8) or other similar attestation approved by Acra.” The excerpt's §8.4 also refers to consumer transactions (PLAT-8.2); whether every loan on this program is a business-purpose transaction: Acra confirmation requested → Q-22. \[G §5.32, p. 3; acralending.com/ratesheets\]

PLAT-1.4 Eligible loan purpose types: Purchase, Rate & Term Refinance, Cash-Out Refinance, Delayed Financing. The matrix footnote states “Delayed financing is capped at \$1.5MM”; which matrix column and which cash-in-hand rule apply to delayed financing: Acra confirmation requested → Q-02. \[P: Loan Purpose Requirements; matrix footnote\]

PLAT-1.5 “Debt Service Coverage Ratio (DSCR) Cash-Out Refinance Transactions requires current lease agreement”. \[P: Loan Purpose Requirements\]

PLAT-1.6 “Vacant properties ineligible”. The Seller's Guide provisions on vacant purchases and §10.17 vacant refinances therefore do not apply (Appendix B). \[P: Loan Purpose Requirements\]

condition.purpose: Resolve whether the repatriation requirement applies to eligible borrowers holding funds abroad and what evidence and timing convention apply.

checks: If an eligible borrower holds funds abroad, Acra confirmation requested in Q-11 establishes whether repatriation applies and what evidence and timing convention apply, and any confirmed applicable requirement is met.

ledger.clause:
8.1 Gift funds, funds to close and seasoning
PLAT-8.1 Gift funds, investment property: applicant(s) are required to contribute a portion of their own sourced and seasoned funds to the transaction at a minimum of 10% of the purchase price (PLAT-1.15). \[G §8.7, p. 12\]

PLAT-8.2 Verification of the seasoning of funds to close is required on loans over 70% CLTV for consumer transactions, or business purpose loans where funds to close are over \$50,000 and over 70% CLTV. Whether any loan on this program is a consumer transaction is Q-22. \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

PLAT-8.3 Where the account(s) serving as the source of funds must be verified, verification may include a copy of the borrower's bank statement(s) for the most recent month(s), or a VOD reflecting a current and average balance for the most recent month(s). \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

PLAT-8.4 “All transactions require a minimum of 30-days documentation.” Whether any seasoning period applies to domestic funds beyond this documentation minimum: Acra confirmation requested → Q-11. \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

PLAT-8.5 “In contrast to the above, but consistent with §3.10.1 of this Guide, funds held in a foreign bank / currency will need to be repatriated at minimum three (3) business days prior to Closing”. Foreign nationals are not eligible for this program, but an eligible US citizen or permanent resident may hold funds abroad; the same sentence's 60-day seasoning requirement is stated for Foreign Nationals only and is not restated. Whether the repatriation requirement applies to eligible borrowers holding funds abroad, and what evidence and timing convention apply: Acra confirmation requested → Q-11. \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

PLAT-8.6 “See guidelines for unacceptable source of funds” — the Seller's Guide provision is not reproduced (Appendix B). \[P: Reserve Requirements\]

condition.purpose: Determine whether applicants contribute their own sourced and seasoned funds equal to at least 10% of the purchase price.
steps: Initial Document Review: Review the loan application and available bank statements for the transaction and funds contributed.
Eligibility Verification: Determine whether the property is an investment property.

Validation and Verification: Verify the applicants' own funds are sourced and seasoned, and compare their contribution with 10% of the purchase price. Review gift documentation requirements in the Seller's Guide gift-fund section (Appendix B).
Final Determination: Record whether the own-funds contribution requirement is met; do not treat seller concessions or other contributions as addressed by the Platinum Summary.
checks: For an investment property, applicants contribute their own sourced and seasoned funds equal to at least 10% of the purchase price.

outcomes.criterion: The property is an investment property and the applicants' own sourced and seasoned funds meet the 10% minimum, with applicable gift documentation requirements reviewed.
Required source, seasoning, gift-fund documentation requirements, or Acra confirmation on seller concessions and other contributions remain to be cleared.

ledger.clause:
8.1 Gift funds, funds to close and seasoning
PLAT-8.1 Gift funds, investment property: applicant(s) are required to contribute a portion of their own sourced and seasoned funds to the transaction at a minimum of 10% of the purchase price (PLAT-1.15). \[G §8.7, p. 12\]

PLAT-8.2 Verification of the seasoning of funds to close is required on loans over 70% CLTV for consumer transactions, or business purpose loans where funds to close are over \$50,000 and over 70% CLTV. Whether any loan on this program is a consumer transaction is Q-22. \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

PLAT-8.3 Where the account(s) serving as the source of funds must be verified, verification may include a copy of the borrower's bank statement(s) for the most recent month(s), or a VOD reflecting a current and average balance for the most recent month(s). \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

PLAT-8.4 “All transactions require a minimum of 30-days documentation.” Whether any seasoning period applies to domestic funds beyond this documentation minimum: Acra confirmation requested → Q-11. \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

PLAT-8.5 “In contrast to the above, but consistent with §3.10.1 of this Guide, funds held in a foreign bank / currency will need to be repatriated at minimum three (3) business days prior to Closing”. Foreign nationals are not eligible for this program, but an eligible US citizen or permanent resident may hold funds abroad; the same sentence's 60-day seasoning requirement is stated for Foreign Nationals only and is not restated. Whether the repatriation requirement applies to eligible borrowers holding funds abroad, and what evidence and timing convention apply: Acra confirmation requested → Q-11. \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

PLAT-8.6 “See guidelines for unacceptable source of funds” — the Seller's Guide provision is not reproduced (Appendix B). \[P: Reserve Requirements\]

8.1 Gift funds, funds to close and seasoning
PLAT-8.1 Gift funds, investment property: applicant(s) are required to contribute a portion of their own sourced and seasoned funds to the transaction at a minimum of 10% of the purchase price (PLAT-1.15). \[G §8.7, p. 12\]

PLAT-8.2 Verification of the seasoning of funds to close is required on loans over 70% CLTV for consumer transactions, or business purpose loans where funds to close are over \$50,000 and over 70% CLTV. Whether any loan on this program is a consumer transaction is Q-22. \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

PLAT-8.3 Where the account(s) serving as the source of funds must be verified, verification may include a copy of the borrower's bank statement(s) for the most recent month(s), or a VOD reflecting a current and average balance for the most recent month(s). \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

PLAT-8.4 “All transactions require a minimum of 30-days documentation.” Whether any seasoning period applies to domestic funds beyond this documentation minimum: Acra confirmation requested → Q-11. \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

PLAT-8.5 “In contrast to the above, but consistent with §3.10.1 of this Guide, funds held in a foreign bank / currency will need to be repatriated at minimum three (3) business days prior to Closing”. Foreign nationals are not eligible for this program, but an eligible US citizen or permanent resident may hold funds abroad; the same sentence's 60-day seasoning requirement is stated for Foreign Nationals only and is not restated. Whether the repatriation requirement applies to eligible borrowers holding funds abroad, and what evidence and timing convention apply: Acra confirmation requested → Q-11. \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

PLAT-8.6 “See guidelines for unacceptable source of funds” — the Seller's Guide provision is not reproduced (Appendix B). \[P: Reserve Requirements\]

ledger.clause:
5.1 Entity eligibility and guarantees
PLAT-5.1 Business Entities are eligible for financing on business purpose transactions (investment properties exclusively). \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.2 Acra will lend to, and require that title to the collateral be held, either (i) directly by an individual person(s) or (ii) by an entity acceptable to Acra in its sole discretion. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.3 Acra requires all individuals with direct or indirect ownership ≥ 20% to provide a recourse guarantee (Acra approved, or Exhibit 7) in the case of an entity borrower. All recourse is joint and several in the case of multiple guarantors. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.4 An entity borrower must be a single purpose entity (SPE): “an entity with no assets other than residential investment or rental properties; engaged in the business of owning and operating residential investment or rental properties.” Series limited liability companies are not allowed. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.5 All entities that will hold direct ownership of the subject property and will be on title as a direct owner are required to be a borrowing entity. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.6 Changes to the operating agreement or bylaws with the intent of changing ownership percentages to circumvent required personal guarantors will not be considered. “Lookback to changes cannot occur within 30 days prior to an Application Date or throughout the application process as these changes will not be recognized by Acra Lending.” \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.7 Entity / guarantor types allowed: Domestic Corporations (C and S Corp); single purpose Limited Liability Companies (LLC), excluding series LLC; Limited Liability Partnership (LLP); Limited Liability Limited Partnership (LLLP); General Partnership (GP); Limited Partnership (LP); and Sole Proprietorship. “In all events, the Borrower must be a US formed and based Entity, foreign entities (i.e.: entities formed or based outside the US) or foreign owned entities are not allowed.” \[G §3.12, p. 8\]
