ledger.clause:
5.3 Due diligence and background checks
PLAT-5.11 Borrower / Guarantor Due Diligence as described above is required to be current as of the date of any loan approval or draw. \[G §3.12, p. 9\]

PLAT-5.12 Acra reviews the background of the Key Principals and Entities: in the case of entity borrowers, the entity, the recourse guarantor(s), and any party (individual or entity) that owns 20% or more of the entity directly or indirectly or has managing control; in the case of individual borrowers, all such individuals. Acra may order background checks on all Key Principals and Entities from Checkpoint, LexisNexis or another comparable provider, including criminal history, OFAC searches, litigation, judgment, and lien searches. \[G §3.12, p. 9\]

clause_parts.heading: 5.3 Due diligence and background checks
clause_parts.text:
PLAT-5.11 Borrower / Guarantor Due Diligence as described above is required to be current as of the date of any loan approval or draw. \[G §3.12, p. 9\]

PLAT-5.12 Acra reviews the background of the Key Principals and Entities: in the case of entity borrowers, the entity, the recourse guarantor(s), and any party (individual or entity) that owns 20% or more of the entity directly or indirectly or has managing control; in the case of individual borrowers, all such individuals. Acra may order background checks on all Key Principals and Entities from Checkpoint, LexisNexis or another comparable provider, including criminal history, OFAC searches, litigation, judgment, and lien searches. \[G §3.12, p. 9\]

ledger.clause:
5.1 Entity eligibility and guarantees
PLAT-5.1 Business Entities are eligible for financing on business purpose transactions (investment properties exclusively). \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.2 Acra will lend to, and require that title to the collateral be held, either (i) directly by an individual person(s) or (ii) by an entity acceptable to Acra in its sole discretion. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.3 Acra requires all individuals with direct or indirect ownership ≥ 20% to provide a recourse guarantee (Acra approved, or Exhibit 7) in the case of an entity borrower. All recourse is joint and several in the case of multiple guarantors. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.4 An entity borrower must be a single purpose entity (SPE): “an entity with no assets other than residential investment or rental properties; engaged in the business of owning and operating residential investment or rental properties.” Series limited liability companies are not allowed. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.5 All entities that will hold direct ownership of the subject property and will be on title as a direct owner are required to be a borrowing entity. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.6 Changes to the operating agreement or bylaws with the intent of changing ownership percentages to circumvent required personal guarantors will not be considered. “Lookback to changes cannot occur within 30 days prior to an Application Date or throughout the application process as these changes will not be recognized by Acra Lending.” \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.7 Entity / guarantor types allowed: Domestic Corporations (C and S Corp); single purpose Limited Liability Companies (LLC), excluding series LLC; Limited Liability Partnership (LLP); Limited Liability Limited Partnership (LLLP); General Partnership (GP); Limited Partnership (LP); and Sole Proprietorship. “In all events, the Borrower must be a US formed and based Entity, foreign entities (i.e.: entities formed or based outside the US) or foreign owned entities are not allowed.” \[G §3.12, p. 8\]

condition.purpose: Determine whether the required entity documentation is provided without exception and contains the specified information.
steps: Initial Document Review: Review entity_documents and identify the entity’s legal form and applicable documentation alternatives.
Eligibility Verification: Apply the stated document requirements without exception; do not accept borrower letters stating that required documents are not required, available, or excused.
Validation and Verification: Verify each applicable required document and its specified content.
Final Determination: Decide whether the required entity documentation is complete; refer any stated Legal discretion to condition for additional supporting documentation separately.
checks: A complete, legible copy of the Certificate of Formation / Articles of Organization and all amendments thereto is provided.

For LLCs and Partnerships, a complete (with all referenced exhibits), legible copy of the Operating Agreement is provided; for corporations, a complete (with all referenced exhibits), legible copy of the Bylaws is provided; applicable amendments are included; the document states whether the entity is member or manager managed, contains authorization to borrow money and enter into contracts for mortgage assets, and designates signers.

All documentation evidencing ownership interests is provided: for LLCs and Partnerships, the Operating Agreement identifies, or attaches as an exhibit, all persons by name with their ownership interest, or copies of membership interest certificates / units in compliance with the Operating Agreement are provided.

For S or C Corporations, shareholder / stockholder certificates that comply with the Bylaws, if any, are provided; if stock certificates are lost or unavailable, the corporation's stock ledger is provided; the certificate or ledger accounts for all outstanding shares noted in the Certificate of Formation / Articles of Organization, including those held by the corporation; if stock certificates are lost, destroyed, mutilated, or otherwise unavailable, an Affidavit of Lost Stock Certificate is provided.

For S-corporations or Partnerships where both stock certificate and stock ledger are unavailable, the most recent preceding tax year's K-1 statement for all members with 20% or more interest is provided, and a letter from the CPA or Tax Preparer affirming current ownership interest is provided, with a statement to that effect if the preceding year's taxes have not been filed.
Names on the entity documents match the identification; if they do not match exactly, a letter of explanation addressing the discrepancy is provided.
A Certificate of Good Standing or equivalent document valid within ninety (90) days of the closing date is provided.

If the entity is formed in a state other than where business is performed or where the property is located, a Certificate of Foreign Qualification or other qualification to operate in the state where business is being conducted is provided.

condition.purpose: Determine whether title vesting in an inter vivos revocable trust satisfies all stated trust requirements.
steps: Initial Document Review: Review the trust or Certification of Trust, title commitment, and any written exception or supporting documents.
Eligibility Verification: Determine whether title is to vest in an inter vivos revocable trust and identify the trustors, trustees, beneficiaries, and required signers.
Validation and Verification: Verify each stated trust-document, validity, revocability, establishment, beneficiary, exception, trustee-power, lender-rights, and additional-documentation requirement.
Final Determination: Decide whether all applicable trust requirements are met and clear any condition for additional supporting documentation.
checks: A complete, legible copy of the Trust, or a Certification of Trust, states the existence and date of the Trust; the Trustor(s) and current Trustee(s); the powers of the Trustee; whether the Trust is revocable and, if revocable, who holds the right to revoke; the names and number of the Trustees required to sign on behalf of the Trust; the Trust identification number (a Social Security number or an IRS-issued Tax Identification Number); how title to the Trust assets should be taken; and that the Trust has not been revoked, modified, or amended in any manner.
The Trust is valid under the laws of the state in which it is established.
The Trust is revocable, meaning it can be changed or canceled at any time for any reason during a Trustor's lifetime; it is not an irrevocable trust.
The Trust is established by one or more natural persons, solely or jointly (Grantor, Trustor, or Settlor), and becomes effective during the lifetime of the person(s) establishing it.
The primary beneficiary of the Trust is the individual(s) establishing the Trust.
Written exception by Acra Senior Management is obtained if the Trustor(s) and Trustee(s) are not the same.

The Trust specifies that the Trustee has the power to hold title and mortgage the property; that the beneficiary does not need to grant written consent for the Trust to borrow money, or that such consent has been granted in writing for purposes of the mortgage; that there is no unusual risk or impairment to the lender's rights; and that holding title in the Trust does not diminish the lender's rights as a creditor.
Any additional supporting documentation for which Legal conditions under its sole discretion is provided.

5.4 Revocable living trusts
PLAT-5.13 Title vesting in an inter vivos revocable trust is permitted when all of the following requirements are followed. \[G §3.12, pp. 9–10\]

- A complete, legible copy of the Trust, or a Certification of Trust stating: the existence and date of the Trust; the Trustor(s) and the current Trustee(s); the powers of the Trustee; whether the Trust is revocable and, if revocable, who holds the right to revoke; the names and number of the Trustees required to sign on behalf of the Trust; the Trust identification number (a Social Security number or an IRS-issued Tax Identification Number); how title to the Trust assets should be taken; and a statement that the Trust has not been revoked, modified, or amended in any manner.

- The Trust must be valid under the laws of the state in which it is established.

- The Trust must be revocable, meaning it can be changed or canceled at any time for any reason during a Trustor's lifetime. Irrevocable trust is not permitted.

- The Trust must be established by one or more natural persons, solely or jointly (Grantor, Trustor, or Settlor), and must become effective during the lifetime of the person(s) establishing it.

- The primary beneficiary of the Trust must be the individual(s) establishing the Trust.

- Written exception by Acra Senior Management must be obtained if the Trustor(s) and Trustee(s) are not the same.

- The Trust must specify that the Trustee has the power to hold title and mortgage the property; that the beneficiary does not need to grant written consent for the Trust to borrow money, or that such consent has been granted in writing for purposes of the mortgage; that there is no unusual risk or impairment to the lender's rights; and that holding title in the Trust does not diminish the lender's rights as a creditor.

- Legal reserves the right to condition for additional supporting documentation as determined in its sole discretion.

5.1 Entity eligibility and guarantees
PLAT-5.1 Business Entities are eligible for financing on business purpose transactions (investment properties exclusively). \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.2 Acra will lend to, and require that title to the collateral be held, either (i) directly by an individual person(s) or (ii) by an entity acceptable to Acra in its sole discretion. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.3 Acra requires all individuals with direct or indirect ownership ≥ 20% to provide a recourse guarantee (Acra approved, or Exhibit 7) in the case of an entity borrower. All recourse is joint and several in the case of multiple guarantors. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.4 An entity borrower must be a single purpose entity (SPE): “an entity with no assets other than residential investment or rental properties; engaged in the business of owning and operating residential investment or rental properties.” Series limited liability companies are not allowed. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.5 All entities that will hold direct ownership of the subject property and will be on title as a direct owner are required to be a borrowing entity. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.6 Changes to the operating agreement or bylaws with the intent of changing ownership percentages to circumvent required personal guarantors will not be considered. “Lookback to changes cannot occur within 30 days prior to an Application Date or throughout the application process as these changes will not be recognized by Acra Lending.” \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.7 Entity / guarantor types allowed: Domestic Corporations (C and S Corp); single purpose Limited Liability Companies (LLC), excluding series LLC; Limited Liability Partnership (LLP); Limited Liability Limited Partnership (LLLP); General Partnership (GP); Limited Partnership (LP); and Sole Proprietorship. “In all events, the Borrower must be a US formed and based Entity, foreign entities (i.e.: entities formed or based outside the US) or foreign owned entities are not allowed.” \[G §3.12, p. 8\]

condition.purpose: Record the stated reserve trigger and preserve Q-08's unresolved combination, calculation, source, and cumulative-trigger questions.
steps: Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Review the loan application and underwriting information for CLTV, reserves, and any separately stated caps or reserve triggers.
Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: Identify whether CLTV is greater than 75.00%; the source states “6-months Reserves required for CLTV > 75.00%”.

Step 3 - Validation and Verification: For CLTV greater than 75.00%, verify six months of reserves. Do not determine how multiple CLTV caps combine, how the declining-market -5% adjustment combines with fixed caps, whether a base reserve requirement applies at CLTV of 75.00% or below, which payment reserves use, permitted reserve sources, whether overlapping reserve triggers are cumulative, or whether reserves are additional to rent loss insurance; Q-08 asks for confirmation on these points.

6.1 Decisioning score and tradelines
PLAT-6.1 “Decisioning Credit Score: Primary Wage Earner middle score. For loans that close in the name of an entity, use the highest middle score of the personal guarantors, presuming equal percentages of ownership. If ownership percentages differ, use the individual with the highest concentration of ownership.” \[P: Borrower Credit History Requirements\]

PLAT-6.2 Minimum decisioning score 700 (no matrix row below 700, PLAT-2.1); Correspondent pricing limited to 60% CLTV for 700-719 (PLAT-2.3). \[P: matrix; footnote 3\]

PLAT-6.3 “Tradelines: Applicants with scores from 3 repositories are deemed to be acceptable with no tradeline overlay. 2 tradelines & 24 month history or 3 tradelines & 12 month history for applicants with 2 or fewer scores.” \[P: Borrower Credit History Requirements\]

PLAT-6.4 Applicants with one score are within “2 or fewer scores” for the tradeline requirement above. The Platinum Summary does not state how the decisioning score is set with one score or with two scores, whether any no-score pathway exists, or how “Primary Wage Earner” is identified on a file with no income documentation. The Standard Summary's one-or-no-score provision is not restated here: Acra confirmation requested → Q-05. \[P: Borrower Credit History Requirements\]

PLAT-6.5 Where two or more guarantors hold an equal largest ownership interest and ownership is not equal across all guarantors, PLAT-6.1 does not say whose score is used: Acra confirmation requested → Q-05. \[P: Borrower Credit History Requirements\]

condition.purpose: Determine the decisioning credit score under PLAT-6.1 and identify cases the source leaves unresolved.
steps: Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Review the loan application, credit report, and, for an entity loan, entity documents for the applicant, personal guarantors, and ownership information relevant to score selection.

Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: Apply PLAT-6.1: use the Primary Wage Earner middle score; for an entity loan, use the highest middle score of personal guarantors when ownership percentages are equal, and otherwise use the individual with the highest concentration of ownership.

Step 3 - Validation and Verification: Check whether the file has one score, two scores, no score, no documented income from which to identify the Primary Wage Earner, or a tie between two or more guarantors for the largest ownership interest when ownership is not equal across all guarantors.

Step 4 - Final Determination: Record the score when the stated rule identifies it; where the source leaves score selection unresolved, mark the determination conditional pending Acra confirmation Q-05.
checks: The decisioning credit score is selected using the PLAT-6.1 rule for the borrower or entity guarantors.
Any one-score, two-score, no-score, undocumented-Primary-Wage-Earner, or specified tied-ownership case is identified as unresolved pending Acra confirmation Q-05.

condition.purpose: Apply the DSCR-specific housing-history documentation scope.
steps: Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Review the file for the subject property, primary residence, second homes, other properties, and documents suggesting a major credit event.
Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: Determine whether the loan is a DSCR loan and identify whether the borrower and/or guarantor(s) have a second home.

Step 3 - Validation and Verification: For a DSCR loan, verify payment-history documentation for the primary residence, subject property, and second homes, if applicable. Do not require documentation for additional properties unless documents in the file suggest a major credit event has occurred.
Step 4 - Final Determination: Record whether the required DSCR payment-history documentation is present and evaluated.
checks: For a DSCR loan, payment history is documented for the primary residence and subject property.
For a DSCR loan, payment history is documented for second homes, if applicable.
Additional properties are not required to have documented housing history unless documents in the file suggest a major credit event has occurred.

ledger.clause:
6.3 Mortgage / rental rating and payment history
PLAT-6.10 The mortgage / rental rating for determining mortgage pricing is determined by evaluating the ratings for properties the borrower owns and / or rents over the last twelve (12) months. All reported mortgages on credit should be considered; where the applicant has mortgages that are not reported, the file should contain documentation to evaluate history on the applicant's primary residence(s), any secondary residence(s), and the subject property. \[G §4.15, p. 5\]

PLAT-6.11 DSCR loans only require documentation on the subject property, principal residence, and second home (if any) of the borrower and / or guarantor(s). Additional properties do not require housing history to be documented unless documents in the file suggest a major credit event has occurred, for example a foreclosure listing the borrower (individually or as guarantor) on the credit report. For DSCR loans, the payment history is required for the primary residence, subject property, and second homes, if applicable. \[G §4.15, p. 5; §6.7, p. 6\]

PLAT-6.12 Loans that have matured are rated based on the maturity date of the loan; any extensions of the maturity date must be in writing. \[G §4.15, p. 5\]

6.2 Housing history and previous credit events
PLAT-6.6 Housing History: “0x30x12”. \[P: Borrower Credit History Requirements\]

PLAT-6.7 The label is reproduced as printed; its definition, and that of “0x30x24” in the escrow-waiver panel: Acra confirmation requested → Q-06. \[P: Borrower Credit History Requirements\]

PLAT-6.8 Previous Credit Events (PCEs): “48 Mo Seasoning”. Which events are covered, the starting event and ending date, the month-counting convention, and the treatment of modifications and forbearance: Acra confirmation requested → Q-06. \[P: Borrower Credit History Requirements\]

PLAT-6.9 “First Time Homebuyer (FTHB) ineligible for this program” (PLAT-4.4). \[P: Borrower Credit History Requirements\]

4. Borrower eligibility
The Platinum Summary lists two eligible citizenship types and excludes first-time homebuyers. Borrowing entities, guarantors and trusts follow the Seller's Guide excerpt and are in section 5.

PLAT-4.1 Eligible borrower citizenship types: US Citizen, Permanent Resident. \[P: Borrower Citizenship Requirements\]

PLAT-4.2 Permanent Resident must have an unexpired PRA ID and SSA card / SSA-89. \[P: Borrower Citizenship Requirements\]

PLAT-4.3 Non-permanent residents, foreign nationals and ITIN borrowers are not among the listed eligible types. The Seller's Guide foreign-national program (§3.10) is therefore not restated (Appendix B). \[P: Borrower Citizenship Requirements\]

PLAT-4.4 “First Time Homebuyer (FTHB) ineligible for this program”. Acra defines a First Time Home Buyer as “an application where all Applicants have never previously owned a home (real property)”; the §3.13 DSCR allowance for first-time homebuyers is not restated (Appendix B). \[P: Borrower Credit History Requirements; G §3.13, p. 10\]

PLAT-4.5 §3.12 requires at least one guarantor to have prior homeownership experience, and at least one borrower / guarantor to attest on the application that they are not a first-time homebuyer (PLAT-5.9). Whether it applies to individual borrowers as well as entities is part of Q-13. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

B.1 Provisions of the excerpt not restated because the Platinum Summary makes them inapplicable
Each exclusion below follows from an express statement in the Platinum Summary, quoted in the middle column. Acra is asked to confirm each (Q-13, Q-20). Provisions the Summary neither excludes nor addresses are listed separately in B.2 and are asked, not excluded.

| **Excerpt provision** | **Platinum Summary statement relied on** | **Effect in this document** |
|----|----|----|
| §3.10 Foreign Nationals (eligibility, documentation, credit references, closing documents) | “Eligible Borrower Citizenship Types: US Citizen, Permanent Resident” | Not restated (PLAT-4.3) |
| §3.13 First Time Home Buyer — DSCR conditions | “First Time Homebuyer (FTHB) ineligible for this program” | Definition kept at PLAT-4.4; conditions not restated |
| §10.17 Vacant Properties; §5.32 and §5.30–5.31 vacant-purchase rent rules | “Vacant properties ineligible” | Not restated (PLAT-1.6, 7.5) |
| §14.13 Short-Term Rental; §5.32 short-term rental ledgers and caps | “Short-Term Rentals (STR) ineligible”; actual-rent rule “applies to long-term rents only” | Not restated (PLAT-3.3) |

6.3 Mortgage / rental rating and payment history
PLAT-6.10 The mortgage / rental rating for determining mortgage pricing is determined by evaluating the ratings for properties the borrower owns and / or rents over the last twelve (12) months. All reported mortgages on credit should be considered; where the applicant has mortgages that are not reported, the file should contain documentation to evaluate history on the applicant's primary residence(s), any secondary residence(s), and the subject property. \[G §4.15, p. 5\]

PLAT-6.11 DSCR loans only require documentation on the subject property, principal residence, and second home (if any) of the borrower and / or guarantor(s). Additional properties do not require housing history to be documented unless documents in the file suggest a major credit event has occurred, for example a foreclosure listing the borrower (individually or as guarantor) on the credit report. For DSCR loans, the payment history is required for the primary residence, subject property, and second homes, if applicable. \[G §4.15, p. 5; §6.7, p. 6\]

PLAT-6.12 Loans that have matured are rated based on the maturity date of the loan; any extensions of the maturity date must be in writing. \[G §4.15, p. 5\]

ledger.clause:
6.3 Mortgage / rental rating and payment history
PLAT-6.10 The mortgage / rental rating for determining mortgage pricing is determined by evaluating the ratings for properties the borrower owns and / or rents over the last twelve (12) months. All reported mortgages on credit should be considered; where the applicant has mortgages that are not reported, the file should contain documentation to evaluate history on the applicant's primary residence(s), any secondary residence(s), and the subject property. \[G §4.15, p. 5\]

PLAT-6.11 DSCR loans only require documentation on the subject property, principal residence, and second home (if any) of the borrower and / or guarantor(s). Additional properties do not require housing history to be documented unless documents in the file suggest a major credit event has occurred, for example a foreclosure listing the borrower (individually or as guarantor) on the credit report. For DSCR loans, the payment history is required for the primary residence, subject property, and second homes, if applicable. \[G §4.15, p. 5; §6.7, p. 6\]

PLAT-6.12 Loans that have matured are rated based on the maturity date of the loan; any extensions of the maturity date must be in writing. \[G §4.15, p. 5\]

steps: Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Review the credit report for repository score count, tradelines, and history.
Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: Determine whether the applicant has scores from 3 repositories or 2 or fewer scores.
Step 3 - Validation and Verification: For scores from 3 repositories, apply no tradeline overlay; for 2 or fewer scores, verify 2 tradelines & 24 month history or 3 tradelines & 12 month history.
Step 4 - Final Determination: Record whether the applicable tradeline requirement is met.
checks: An applicant with scores from 3 repositories is not subjected to a tradeline overlay.
An applicant with 2 or fewer scores meets 2 tradelines & 24 month history or 3 tradelines & 12 month history.

outcomes.criterion: The applicant has scores from 3 repositories, or the applicable requirement for 2 or fewer scores is met.
There is no case for this outcome.
The applicant has 2 or fewer scores and meets neither stated tradeline-and-history alternative.
There is no case for this outcome.

ledger.clause:
6.1 Decisioning score and tradelines
PLAT-6.1 “Decisioning Credit Score: Primary Wage Earner middle score. For loans that close in the name of an entity, use the highest middle score of the personal guarantors, presuming equal percentages of ownership. If ownership percentages differ, use the individual with the highest concentration of ownership.” \[P: Borrower Credit History Requirements\]

PLAT-6.2 Minimum decisioning score 700 (no matrix row below 700, PLAT-2.1); Correspondent pricing limited to 60% CLTV for 700-719 (PLAT-2.3). \[P: matrix; footnote 3\]

PLAT-6.3 “Tradelines: Applicants with scores from 3 repositories are deemed to be acceptable with no tradeline overlay. 2 tradelines & 24 month history or 3 tradelines & 12 month history for applicants with 2 or fewer scores.” \[P: Borrower Credit History Requirements\]

PLAT-6.4 Applicants with one score are within “2 or fewer scores” for the tradeline requirement above. The Platinum Summary does not state how the decisioning score is set with one score or with two scores, whether any no-score pathway exists, or how “Primary Wage Earner” is identified on a file with no income documentation. The Standard Summary's one-or-no-score provision is not restated here: Acra confirmation requested → Q-05. \[P: Borrower Credit History Requirements\]

PLAT-6.5 Where two or more guarantors hold an equal largest ownership interest and ownership is not equal across all guarantors, PLAT-6.1 does not say whose score is used: Acra confirmation requested → Q-05. \[P: Borrower Credit History Requirements\]

6. Credit requirements
The Platinum Summary defines the decisioning score, the tradeline requirements, a single housing-history standard and a single seasoning requirement for previous credit events. The Seller's Guide provisions on mortgage / rental rating follow.

condition.purpose: Preserve the unresolved Q-07 property-feature questions without adding eligibility rules.
steps: Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Review the loan application and property information for property type, unit count, rural status, and mixed-use, Adult Care, Assisted Living, or PUDtel features.

Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: Compare the property information with Q-07's stated eligible list (SFR, Townhome, PUD, Warrantable Condo, Two-Units) and ineligible list (Rural, Condotels, Non-Warrantable Condos, STR).

Step 3 - Validation and Verification: For three- and four-unit properties, manufactured homes, mixed-use / Adult Care / Assisted Living, and PUDtels, retain the source's question whether they are ineligible or addressed elsewhere; do not resolve it by assumption.
Step 4 - Final Determination: Record a conditional result when a Q-07 category affects the case and Acra's answer is outstanding.
checks: The Q-07 eligible and ineligible lists are applied as printed.
A case involving three- or four-unit properties, manufactured homes, mixed-use / Adult Care / Assisted Living, or PUDtels is identified as unresolved pending Acra confirmation Q-07.

outcomes.criterion: The case does not depend on an unresolved Q-07 category, and any applicable printed eligible or ineligible list item is treated as printed.
The case depends on whether a queried Q-07 property category is ineligible or addressed elsewhere, and Acra confirmation is outstanding.
The property is Rural, a Condotel, a Non-Warrantable Condo, or STR, as listed as ineligible.
There is no property to which the Platinum property-feature provisions apply.

steps: Initial Document Review: Review the loan application for each borrower's stated citizenship type.

Eligibility Verification: Determine whether each borrower's type is US Citizen or Permanent Resident; non-permanent residents, foreign nationals and ITIN borrowers are not among the listed eligible types.

Final Determination: Record whether every borrower has a listed eligible citizenship type.

There is no case for this outcome.
At least one borrower's citizenship type is not US Citizen or Permanent Resident, or is a non-permanent resident, foreign national or ITIN borrower.
There is no case for this outcome.

ledger.clause:
4. Borrower eligibility
The Platinum Summary lists two eligible citizenship types and excludes first-time homebuyers. Borrowing entities, guarantors and trusts follow the Seller's Guide excerpt and are in section 5.

PLAT-4.1 Eligible borrower citizenship types: US Citizen, Permanent Resident. \[P: Borrower Citizenship Requirements\]

PLAT-4.2 Permanent Resident must have an unexpired PRA ID and SSA card / SSA-89. \[P: Borrower Citizenship Requirements\]

PLAT-4.3 Non-permanent residents, foreign nationals and ITIN borrowers are not among the listed eligible types. The Seller's Guide foreign-national program (§3.10) is therefore not restated (Appendix B). \[P: Borrower Citizenship Requirements\]

PLAT-4.4 “First Time Homebuyer (FTHB) ineligible for this program”. Acra defines a First Time Home Buyer as “an application where all Applicants have never previously owned a home (real property)”; the §3.13 DSCR allowance for first-time homebuyers is not restated (Appendix B). \[P: Borrower Credit History Requirements; G §3.13, p. 10\]

PLAT-4.5 §3.12 requires at least one guarantor to have prior homeownership experience, and at least one borrower / guarantor to attest on the application that they are not a first-time homebuyer (PLAT-5.9). Whether it applies to individual borrowers as well as entities is part of Q-13. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

B.1 Provisions of the excerpt not restated because the Platinum Summary makes them inapplicable
Each exclusion below follows from an express statement in the Platinum Summary, quoted in the middle column. Acra is asked to confirm each (Q-13, Q-20). Provisions the Summary neither excludes nor addresses are listed separately in B.2 and are asked, not excluded.

| **Excerpt provision** | **Platinum Summary statement relied on** | **Effect in this document** |
|----|----|----|
| §3.10 Foreign Nationals (eligibility, documentation, credit references, closing documents) | “Eligible Borrower Citizenship Types: US Citizen, Permanent Resident” | Not restated (PLAT-4.3) |
| §3.13 First Time Home Buyer — DSCR conditions | “First Time Homebuyer (FTHB) ineligible for this program” | Definition kept at PLAT-4.4; conditions not restated |
| §10.17 Vacant Properties; §5.32 and §5.30–5.31 vacant-purchase rent rules | “Vacant properties ineligible” | Not restated (PLAT-1.6, 7.5) |
| §14.13 Short-Term Rental; §5.32 short-term rental ledgers and caps | “Short-Term Rentals (STR) ineligible”; actual-rent rule “applies to long-term rents only” | Not restated (PLAT-3.3) |

PLAT-1.7 The program is offered through two channels with different minimum ratios: Correspondent ≥ 1.2, Wholesale ≥ 1.0 (PLAT-3.7). Matrix footnote 3 also restricts Correspondent pricing (PLAT-2.3). \[P: Minimum DSCR; matrix footnote 3\]

PLAT-1.8 Every loan must meet the applicable channel minimum DSCR. The Platinum Summary lists no No Ratio option and no allowance for a ratio below 1.0; a ratio below the channel minimum does not meet the published requirement. Whether No Ratio or sub-1.0 qualification exists on this program in any form: Acra confirmation requested → Q-12. \[P: Minimum DSCR\]

PLAT-1.9 Acra will not calculate a DTI for applicants who qualify using a DSCR; income or employment listed on an application is superfluous to the underwrite and may be left blank, and if represented, a DTI should not be calculated. The Standard Summary's statement that borrowing-entity income documentation is not required does not appear in the Platinum Summary; whether it applies: Acra confirmation requested → Q-13. \[G §7.3, p. 5\]

PLAT-1.10 “A 1007 will always be required on DSCR transactions”; the Platinum Summary refers to market rent “as established on the 1007 or 1025”. Whether a Form 1025 alone satisfies the requirement for a two-unit property: Acra confirmation requested → Q-04. \[G §5.32, p. 3; §14.12, p. 4; P: Income Documentation\]

PLAT-1.11 All borrowers purchasing or refinancing a one- to four-family investment property must execute a One- to Four-Family Rider with the loan documents and provide rent loss insurance coverage per §23.40 (PLAT-7.9 to 7.12). \[G §3.41, p. 11\]

PLAT-1.12 Only the subject property, principal residence and second homes are required to be listed on the application or Schedule of Real Estate Owned. \[G §5.32, p. 3; §4.15, p. 5\]

condition.purpose: Use the greater of market rent established on the 1007 or 1025, or actual rent, subject to the stated conditions for using actual rent.
steps: Initial Document Review: Review the 1007 or 1025, lease, and evidence of rental receipts.
Eligibility Verification: Establish whether the proposed rent is long-term or short-term rental income.

Validation and Verification: For long-term rental income, compare market rent established on the 1007 or 1025 with actual rent and use the greater. When actual rent is used, verify evidence of 2 months’ proof of receipts and that the lease is in place for at least 3 months after the loan closing. Apply the Platinum Summary wording; the relationship to the Seller's Guide wording, whether the two months must be consecutive, and whether the security-deposit and prepaid-rent conditions apply are identified as matters awaiting Acra confirmation, not additional resolved requirements.
Final Determination: Record the qualifying rent basis and amount, and whether the stated conditions for using actual rent are met.
checks: For long-term rent, the qualifying rent is the greater of market rent established on the 1007 or 1025 and actual rent.
When actual rent is used, it is documented via evidence of 2 months’ proof of receipts and the lease is in place for at least 3 months after the loan closing.

outcomes.criterion: The qualifying rent uses the greater of market rent and actual rent, and, when actual rent is used, both stated documentation and lease-duration conditions are met.
Rent evidence or lease-duration information required to determine the qualifying rent remains to be obtained or verified.
The qualifying rent does not use the stated greater-of rule, or actual rent is used without either stated condition being met.
There is no case for this outcome.

ledger.clause:
3.1 Qualifying rent, as printed in the Platinum Summary
PLAT-3.1 “When calculating the DSCR, Acra will use the greater of the market rent as established on the 1007 or 1025, or actual rent. When using actual rent, the actual rent must be documented via evidence of 2 months’ proof of receipts and the lease must be in place for at least 3 months after the loan closing. This applies to long-term rents only and is not appropriate for short-term rentals.” \[P: Income Documentation & Debt Ratio Requirements\]

PLAT-3.2 §5.32 of the excerpt states the general formula as “the lesser of (i) annual in-place rent or (ii) market rent”, then notes that “Acra may use the higher of actual or market rents” subject to “two (2) consecutive months proof of rental income receipt”, a lease continuing at least three months after closing, and: “Security Deposit does not count towards receipt, and the rents cannot be prepaid.” The Platinum Summary's statement (PLAT-3.1) is program-specific; the excerpt's general formula is reproduced here. Which governs Platinum Select and how they relate, whether “2 months’ proof of receipts” means consecutive months, and whether the security-deposit and prepaid-rent conditions apply: Acra confirmation requested → Q-03. \[G §5.32, p. 3\]

PLAT-3.3 Short-term rentals are ineligible for the program (PLAT-7.2); the Seller's Guide provisions on short-term rental income and appraisal forms are not restated (Appendix B). \[P: Subject Property Requirements\]

3. DSCR calculation and rental income
The Platinum Summary states its own rule for qualifying rent; the Seller's Guide excerpt supplies the denominator, the payment used, the rent-schedule requirements and the treatment of applicants with recent forbearance or lates. Both are quoted where they differ.

condition.purpose: Check the Seller's Guide excerpt provision for tenant-occupied properties while preserving the source's stated uncertainty about how it relates to Platinum Select's 0x30x12 requirement.
steps: Initial Document Review: Review the credit report and, where applicable, rental-payment and reserve documentation.
Eligibility Verification: Establish whether the property is tenant occupied and whether the Applicant has had forbearance or mortgage lates within the last 12-months.

Validation and Verification: For a tenant occupied property meeting that stated condition, verify either timely receipt for the prior two (2) months rental payments or 12-months of the subject's payment in reserve, which may be from transaction's cash-in-hand. Separately note that the Platinum Summary requires “0x30x12”; the sources do not state how the provisions relate, whether the alternatives apply on Platinum Select where a late exists, which cases they cover, or whether “Applicant” includes guarantors of an entity borrower.
Final Determination: Record the evidence for the stated alternatives and leave the identified relationship and applicability questions unresolved unless confirmed.

ledger.clause:
7.4 Rent loss insurance (§23.40)
PLAT-7.9 Rent loss insurance covers rental losses that are incurred during the period that a property is being rehabilitated following a casualty. \[G §23.40, p. 13\]

PLAT-7.10 Six (6) months' rent loss insurance is required on one- to four-unit non-owner occupied income properties with LTV \> 70% and when subject property rents are used to qualify. \[G §23.40, p. 13\]

PLAT-7.11 “Loans with ≤ 70% CLTV are not required to carry rent loss insurance.” The requirement is stated in LTV and the exemption in CLTV; the case of LTV at or below 70% with CLTV above 70%: Acra confirmation requested → Q-10. \[G §23.40, p. 13\]

PLAT-7.12 When rent loss insurance is required but cannot be obtained, the borrower may substitute two (2) months reserves for every one (1) month of rent loss coverage not provided. \[G §23.40, p. 13\]

condition.purpose: Verify required rent loss insurance covers rental losses incurred during rehabilitation following a casualty and provides six (6) months' coverage.
steps: Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Review the hazard insurance declarations and identify the rent loss insurance coverage, its duration, and stated coverage terms.

condition.purpose: Determine whether cash in hand meets the printed matrix-footnote limit; the source does not resolve whether the tests use LTV or CLTV.
steps: Initial Document Review: For a Cash-Out transaction, review loan_application for loan amount, LTV, and cash in hand.

Eligibility Verification: Apply the printed footnotes: when LTV > 65%, maximum cash-in-hand is $1,000,000 for loans ≥ $1,500,000 and $500,000 for loans < $1,500,000; when LTV ≤ 65%, unlimited cash-in-hand is allowed.
Validation and Verification: Verify the figures and note that the source states these footnotes in LTV while the matrix is labelled CLTV.
Final Determination: Record whether the printed cash-in-hand limit is met; do not substitute a CLTV test for the source's LTV wording.
checks: For a Cash-Out transaction with LTV > 65%, cash in hand is no more than $1,000,000 when the loan amount is ≥ $1,500,000, or no more than $500,000 when the loan amount is < $1,500,000; when LTV ≤ 65%, the printed rule allows unlimited cash-in-hand.

outcomes.criterion: The transaction is not Cash-Out, or the cash-in-hand amount meets the applicable printed LTV-based rule.
There is no case for this outcome.
The transaction is Cash-Out, LTV is > 65%, and cash in hand exceeds the applicable maximum.
There is no case for this outcome.

1.1 Occupancy, purpose and qualification
PLAT-1.1 Occupancy: Non-Owner Occupied. \[P: Occupancy Requirements\]

PLAT-1.2 An investment property is “a one- to four-unit residential dwelling or a unit in a condominium complex or a PUD owned by an individual who does not occupy the dwelling. The dwelling is leased and occupied as a principal year-round residence to individuals other than the owner.” The property types the Platinum Summary lists as eligible are at PLAT-7.1; types it does not list are set out in the table at 7.1 and asked in Q-07. \[G §3.41, p. 11; P: Subject Property Requirements\]

PLAT-1.3 The Program Summary is listed as “Business Purpose DSCR Platinum” on Acra's rate-sheet page. “Where the borrower is qualifying utilizing the subject property's actual or market cashflow under a business purpose transaction, borrower must execute with loan docs a Business Purpose Attestation (Exhibit 8) or other similar attestation approved by Acra.” The excerpt's §8.4 also refers to consumer transactions (PLAT-8.2); whether every loan on this program is a business-purpose transaction: Acra confirmation requested → Q-22. \[G §5.32, p. 3; acralending.com/ratesheets\]

PLAT-1.4 Eligible loan purpose types: Purchase, Rate & Term Refinance, Cash-Out Refinance, Delayed Financing. The matrix footnote states “Delayed financing is capped at \$1.5MM”; which matrix column and which cash-in-hand rule apply to delayed financing: Acra confirmation requested → Q-02. \[P: Loan Purpose Requirements; matrix footnote\]

PLAT-1.5 “Debt Service Coverage Ratio (DSCR) Cash-Out Refinance Transactions requires current lease agreement”. \[P: Loan Purpose Requirements\]

PLAT-1.6 “Vacant properties ineligible”. The Seller's Guide provisions on vacant purchases and §10.17 vacant refinances therefore do not apply (Appendix B). \[P: Loan Purpose Requirements\]

2.2 Matrix footnotes, quoted
PLAT-2.2 Footnote 1, whose marker is printed on the Cash-Out column heading: “When LTV \> 65% Max Cash-in-Hand: \$1,000,000 for loans ≥ \$1,500,000, \$500,000 for loans \< \$1,500,000.” Footnote 2, whose marker appears nowhere in the matrix: “When LTV ≤ 65%, unlimited cash-in-hand allowed.” The footnotes are stated in LTV while the matrix is labelled CLTV: Acra confirmation requested → Q-16. \[P: matrix footnotes 1–2\]

PLAT-2.3 Footnote 3, whose marker also appears nowhere in the matrix: “Correspondent Pricing limited to 60% CLTV for 700-719 FICO”. For a Correspondent cash-out at 700-719 the matrix already prints 55%; the 60% footnote does not raise that figure. How the two limits apply together by purpose: Acra confirmation requested → Q-01. \[P: matrix footnote 3\]

PLAT-2.4 Footnote \*: “Delayed financing is capped at \$1.5MM” (PLAT-1.4, Q-02). \[P: matrix footnote\]

condition.purpose: Determine whether the requested CLTV is within the applicable matrix maximum, using the printed score thresholds literally.

Validation and Verification: Verify the selected row, column, score, and requested CLTV against the file.
Final Determination: Record whether the requested CLTV is within the selected matrix maximum.

condition.purpose: Determine whether a printed state restriction is triggered by the case facts; the source requests confirmation about what BUY-OUT requires.
steps: Initial Document Review: Review loan_application for state, units, party type, loan amount, note rate, loan purpose, and closing name where applicable.

Eligibility Verification: Check the exact printed triggers: AK—Residential 1-4; IL—Residential 1-4 to an ENTITY OR INDIVIDUAL with loan amount ≤$250,000, or to an INDIVIDUAL with loan amount >$250,000 and interest rate >8%; KS—Residential 1-4; MD—all loans; MI—Residential 1-4; MN—Residential 1-4; MS—Residential 1 unit, or no restriction on 2+ units; NJ—all loans closing in name of an INDIVIDUAL; NM—Residential 1-4; OH—Residential 1-2; PA—INDIVIDUAL, Residential 1-2, and loan amount <$319,777; RI—PURCHASE; VA—Residential 1-4 closed in the name of an individual; VT—loans <$1 Million.
Validation and Verification: Verify each relevant case fact against the loan file. Do not infer what BUY-OUT requires.
Final Determination: Record whether a printed state trigger applies and refer the meaning and consequence of BUY-OUT for clarification.
checks: AK restriction trigger: state is AK and property is Residential 1-4.

IL restriction trigger: state is IL and either the property is Residential 1-4, party is ENTITY OR INDIVIDUAL, and loan amount is ≤$250,000; or the property is Residential 1-4, party is INDIVIDUAL, loan amount is >$250,000, and interest rate is >8%.
KS restriction trigger: state is KS and property is Residential 1-4.
MD restriction trigger: state is MD.
MI restriction trigger: state is MI and property is Residential 1-4.
MN restriction trigger: state is MN and property is Residential 1-4.
MS restriction trigger: state is MS and property is Residential 1 unit; 2+ units have no restriction.
NJ restriction trigger: state is NJ and loan closes in the name of an INDIVIDUAL.
NM restriction trigger: state is NM and property is Residential 1-4.
OH restriction trigger: state is OH and property is Residential 1-2.
PA restriction trigger: state is PA and party is an INDIVIDUAL, property is Residential 1-2, and loan amount is <$319,777.
RI restriction trigger: state is RI and the transaction is a PURCHASE.
VA restriction trigger: state is VA and property is Residential 1-4 closed in the name of an individual.
VT restriction trigger: state is VT and loan amount is <$1 Million.
